title: Many Design Flaws in the Monitor
text:
Do not buy this monitor if you are planning to connect more than one computer to it. You will either be crawling under the desk pulling the display cable so that you can see the display of the other computer or constantly trying to switch to the other computer while booting hoping to catch it at the correct boot moment.
There are two major flaws in the design of this monitor. It is a large monitor and the OCD controls are in the back. This and the fact that there is no way to stop autosense switching input makes it a big pain to connect it to multiple devices. For example, my monitor is connected to a Linux and MAC machine. I wanted to reboot my MAC while pressing command-R key. I had to keep my hand on the keys and stand on one leg and constantly reach the back of the monitor to select the DP port that my MAC is connected until the display came on, otherwise, the display would switch back to the Linux machine. MAC turns off display during power save. The input switches to another port. The support confirmed that there is no way to disable auto sense switching the monitor and the only way is to disconnect the other inputs.
The software does not come with the monitor and it is only for Windows. So, it is useless for my MAC and Linux machines.
If you only connect one Windows machine to this monitor the display is good, but, it is extremely painful to operate because of where they have put the OCD buttons. They put the LED in from where it would be easy to reach, but, the geniuses put the control in the back of the monitor. The crass customer support told me it is for aesthetics. Pitty, that they seem to have no common sense. Otherwise, for the price it would have been a good monitor.

title: It is all I expected it to be!
text:
This is a great case and an excellent value for the money. I don't write product reviews very often, but this is my second Caseology case (previous one was for my Nexus 5 phone, now replaced by my Pixel XL.) I wanted to post this review with photos because some of the earlier reviews were of the black case but the colored ones weren't yet available, and now they are and I bought the rose / copper colored one.

The case has an excellent fit to the Pixel XL and it feels high quality - much better than the $30 clear Google branded case. The grip feels solid but not too sticky in my hand like some of the rubber or silicon cases. I had been worried about dropping this very expensive phone and not having a bit of protection around it, because without a case it is slippery. So now I'm more comfortable with having some basic protection on it. The case is not going to protect the phone like an Otterbox or some other really durable and drop-proof case, but I didn't want a huge case on the phone since I carry it in my pocket.

The build quality of the case seems very good. The outer copper colored section fits accurately over the inner section and all the grooves, cut-outs, and angles between the two sections line up perfectly. As shown in my photos, all the case cut-outs also fit just right over the phone's various holes. The cut-out for the USB C power plug is large enough that my plugs go in with clearance, not rubbing on the case. The phone's power and volume buttons are covered by the case's rubber buttons, so I don't have to stick my finger tip into a hole in the case to turn on the phone or adjust the volume. The case's rubber buttons protrude very slightly from the outer copper colored section, but not so much that the phone gets turned on or the volume adjusted by accident.

I have only had this case for a few days, so we will see how it holds up to normal wear and tear. I'm pretty careful with my phones, so I don't expect it to get banged up or scratched. If it does in spite of my careful use, I will post a future review update. I was very pleased with my Nexus 5 Caseology case which was nearly 3 years old and still looked nice, so I thought I'd give this vendor another try and this case looks really great, works well, and meets my expectations!

title: Great monitor for the price, having DP issues though
text:
UPDATE (Most Recent): I've had the monitor for about a month now since the last update. The issue was fixed by completely unplugging my tower and monitor and just leaving them over night. I've learned to avoid the issue by preventing the computer from going to sleep since I've read that DP has some issues with waking up from sleep mode which is what I think caused my original issue. Occasionally I'll get the "No Signal" issue again and it's usually fixed by just powering down my tower completely and then restarting it.

UPDATE (old): Writing this a few days after my original review, my monitor is having issues getting signal over DP. Windows recognizes the monitor but the monitor shows "No Signal" when I try to turn it on. the HDMI and DVI inputs work perfectly fine but they don't do 144hz, which is what I bought this monitor for. Considering returning or selling this monitor.

This is an affordable option for those looking for a 1080p 144 Hz monitor. I use it for both content creation work and just general gaming and it's been awesome. Visuals seem crisp, colors are pretty good, and overall I'm really happy with it.

Out of the box the monitor is EXTREMELY bright. Like you could light a room with just this monitor. I have my brightness set to 0 in the settings and that feels significantly better to look at for long periods of time.

As one could expect the built in speakers aren't anything great, but I'm incredibly pleased that Acer included an audio out port (3.5mm) on the monitor so you can take the audio from the HDMI or DP inputs and send them to your own speakers.

The monitor has a button to activate "Game Mode" which seems to put some sort of sharpen filter on the screen and I have a feeling it plays a little bit with the colors as well. It also puts an FPS counter in the top right corner but that counter was a constant 144, even when I limited my framerate in games to 60 fps just to test it out so the counter isn't too useful and ultimately I think the Game Mode in general is a pain because of that sharpen filter especially. If you switch to Game Mode and then back to regular mode keep in mind that your monitor settings get reverted back to default, this includes color and brightness. Avoid the Game Mode button and this is a non-issue.

title: Exceptional Performance on Haswell-E, Skylake, and Kaby Lake!
text:
Let me start off by saying the Grand Macho is an absolute MONSTER. Even without a fan installed it's just under twice the size of my Hyper 212 Evo with two fans installed.

On top of that review sites show this cooler defeating the legendary Noctua NH-D15 while also being quieter. So from the beginning my expectations were pretty high.

And to say the Grand Macho didn't disappoint would be an understatement. This cooler absolutely blew my expectations out of the water! I tested it across three different Intel CPUs, with performance consistent across all three platforms.

First, I tested it on my Core i5 6600k. It kept my 6600K so cool that I bumped the overclock from 4.3 Ghz at 1.23 volts and 73C under full load with my old Hyper 212 Evo to 4.8 Ghz at 1.40 volts and 68C under full load with the Grand Macho just because the increase in thermal headroom was much greater.

Next I switched to an i5 7600k that I traded the 6600k for (the owner hated the terrible temperatures of the Kaby Lake CPU), and although I did ultimately delid the CPU due to the terrible temperatures, I did record temperatures both before and after the delid. Before the delid the idle temperature of the 7600k at 4.4 Ghz 1.28 volts was 45 C and the full load temperature was 77 C. After the delid and a 5.1 Ghz overclock at 1.38 volts the idle temps were at 32 C and 64 C under full load. Pretty drastic temperature improvement from a delid, and just another sign of Intel's decline in quality.

Finally, I tried it on a Core i7 5820k with a 4.5 Ghz overclock at 1.31 volts, and this is where the Grand Macho truly shined. 34 C at idle and with a max recorded temperature of 71 C under full load, it's an incredible performer. I actually compared it to the NH-D15 cooler I already had mounted on the motherboard with the same overclock and brand of thermal paste, and it performed with an idle temperature of 37 C and a max recorded temperature at full load of 76 C. Not a massive loss for the NH-D15, but it just speaks for the ability of the Grand Macho.

RAM compatibility is actually pretty great for a cooler this size, and I can still use my Ballistix RAM without any compromises. The Grand Macho also doesn't come anywhere close to interfering with the first PCI-E slot on either motherboard, something my NH-D15 did on the LGA 1151 motherboard.

Installation was a breeze, particularly with the LGA 2011 motherboard. Everything was so simple that I didn't bother to remove either of the motherboards from the case during installation. It also helps that the cooler came with a large magnetic tipped screwdriver (that I will use more in the future) and protective gloves to make installation easier. The only real installation flaw was the fan installation itself, it's tricky to get on there and it will take several attempts to get the fan clips to attach to the cooler.

Overall, I highly recommend this cooler for those of you who want fantastic cooling performance, but are also too fearful of the potential points of failure in liquid cooling to buy an AIO cooler or invest in CLC cooling. It keeps temperatures remarkably low for an air cooler, and with its high compatibility and low height it's perfect for Mid ATX towers such as my NZXT S340.

title: The Lorex Ping app is horrible. Well
text:
I bought this camera to replace my Lorex camera. The Lorex Ping app is horrible. Well, surprise surprise, Samsung's apps are also horrible. Ugh.

First, the Smart Cam is a very pretty camera. It is well made, and looks good wherever it is placed. It does run a little hot, so be careful about placing the camera in a well ventilated area. This is a minor inconvenience.

The field of view is very good, and the picture quality -- both in daylight and at night (IR) is well above average.

However, there are three ways to access the camera: via the web using a PC, using the Android app, and using the Apple (IOS) app. Unfortunately, they are all different ---- they have different capabilities, and the look-and-feel are all different. There really is no reason for this other than sloppiness or incompetence on the part of Samsung's product team. So, to make some setting changes, they must be made via (for example) a PC; to set up a Wifi connection, this must be done via one of the mobile apps. Why?? And the user documentation (easily downloaded from Samsung's website), isn't well written and is oftentimes incomplete and incorrect. Ugh.

Last, the recorded video files that were written to and saved on the internal SD card cannot be erased one-by-one. The only way to erase one or more files on the SD card is to re-format the SD card. This is completely ridiculous! So saving, for example, a critical video file on the SD card is impossible: all files must be saved/retained on the SD card.......and hopefully the important file won't be overwritten before it is needed.

I still haven't figured out how to move/transfer a video file from the SD card to a PC or to a mobile device. The instructions in the IOS manual don't work.......why am I not surprised.

text:
I have never seen a set of bluetooth speakers that offer a stereo setup. I was a bit skeptical that it might add complexity but these are as simple as a single unit..

There are several good features about the speakers starting with the ability to separate them a distance and offer a true stereo surround sound. They can get very loud and it sounds very good.

You can operate this as two speakers or you can just connect to one of them if you want to be smaller and quieter. When you power on both speakers at the same time they automatically connect to each other and just show as a single unit in your Bluetooth connection. It is extremely simple to connect to them just like you would connect to any other device.

As you can see in the picture each one of the speakers has a plus minus and a pause play button. If you hold down the plus or minus it will change the volume. If you short tap the plus or minus it will move forward or backward in the playlist. The pause button will either pause or resume the music. Since both of the speakers have those buttons you can simply change it on the one that is closest to you.

For storage the speakers have magnets in the bottom and they stick together to keep them as a single unit.

They do support Bluetooth or a line in. These do not have a memory card spot but that is not something that I normally use anyway.

Yuneec has also updated the software so that you can fly a simulated Typhoon H with this simulator. I have to say, I was VERY impressed with how realistic and accurate the simulator was! With the Typhoon H remote you can control all of the basic flight functions of the H, including the landing gear. You can even rotate and pan the camera that is on the simulator. And just like the real thing, you can adjust the speed of the H by the joystick as well as the speed dial.

TAKING OFF NOTE!
One thing that I did have to learn is, in order to take flight, you have to make sure the speed dial is NOT at the slowest setting. This means you will need to push the lever that is on the right side in the front up slightly. You will hear a "beep" when you did this that indicates you are able to take off.

Please note that the simulated camera does NOT broadcast any images! The simulator is not designed for that. It's purpose is to provide flight experience and training.

There are also 3 Challenges in the simulator that grade your performance and allow you to keep track of your progress. My first attempt at Challenge #1 yielded me a 19%, however, after several tries I reached a high of 89%. Because I am an over achiever, I'm pushing for an A!

With this simulator you will DEFINITELY improve your control of your drone. I HIGHLY recommend that anyone who owns a Yuneec drone purchase this!

title: Audiophile quality and tons of connectivity
text:
08/15/2015 Edit 2: Upgraded to Windows 10. Drivers and software have an ETA of the 3rd week of August. Just a heads up to everyone else.
04/15/2015 Edit: Creative Labs has just released a firmware update that fixes a few bugs for people connecting this via USB and a host of other changes, along with that there is a new driver update released almost a day ago. Just a heads up in case people have some lingering issues or want the latest driver update.
=====================================================================================================
I recently purchased the X7 for a X99 build I just completed. I needed an external sound card as the current PCIE slots were all taken thanks to a 3 Way SLI Rig coupled with a M.2.
==========================================================================================================
Box Contents/Packaging
==========================================================================================================

The X7 came nicely packaged, the headphone stand and all other accessories were included. What was surprising was the amount of power cables that were included. There was a cable for every country socket that I could think off, a nice touch. There was a manual, a micro USB to USB cable, a 3.5mm to RCA cable, along with a 3.5mm RCA input cable.

==========================================================================================================
INSTALLATION
==========================================================================================================

Extremely simple, connect all the cables, since I am using this with my PC a USB cable was required. I am pairing the X7 with the Logitech Z906 and it was very simple to connect everything. I was running in 15min. There is no driver CD so the drivers have to be manually downloaded from the creative labs website.

The amount of options for connectivity this DAC has is astounding. Everything from bluetooth, NFC, USB, optical, etc. I could go on, the options are very very impressive. The build quality is also very impressive. The metal volume knob is a nice touch, gives the whole thing a high quality feel. I am also especially fond of the headphone stand. It is large enough to carry headphones such as the Bowers & Wilkins P7 I have on it quite easily.

==========================================================================================================
SOUND QUALITY and FIRST IMPRESSION
==========================================================================================================

Suffice to say these sound leagues better then the built in motherboard sound card (ASUS RAMPAGE EXTREME V) which has apparently a very good one from the factory in the form of the SOUND EXTREME FX. The software from the website was installed without a hitch and I had everything running in minutes. The layout is very simple and provides enough options in case one wishes to modify settings or sound depending on taste.

Took the opportunity and tried it in a few games, namely Dragon Age: Inquisition, Starcraft II, Homeworld I&II Remastered, and Far Cry 4. The sound was crisp and clean, the channel separation in a 5.1 setup was great, one of the main reasons I was unhappy with the built in sound card (motherboard).

I have tested the Bowers and Wilkins P7 with this DAC and I am very pleased with the sound quality that I have experienced. There is a noticeable improvement especially compared to an iPhone or iPod obviously.

I also want to add that there is an app available for both iOS and Android for the X7 which serves as a remote control. I quite like it, allows me to control the DAC remotely.

==========================================================================================================
CONCLUSION
==========================================================================================================

I've only had this for a few weeks and I am quite pleased with it all in all, I have always had a discrete sound card, since the days of the Creative Labs AWE 32 and AWE 64, which was a while ago! Anyone that values sound and requires an external soundcard/DAC should definitely consider this. The sound quality is phenomenal, the DAC itself is stylish and built very nicely and offers loads of connectivity options as well.

RECOMMENDED!

==========================================================================================================

title: Most poor reviews (I star) start with I for IGNORANCE
text:
NOTE TO THE LITERACY OR TECHNOLOGY CHALLENGED - A "charging" port on an OTG cable is used to power the accessories attached to the USB port. The microUSB on most mobile devices will not provide sufficient power to operate a USB flash drive, keyboard or much of anything. Therefore, thoughtful cable providers include a way to power them from another USB source.

I haven't found an OTG cable that claimed to be able to charge the device (except for an internal battery combo that disconnects all other USB devices when using it to charge the device).

Quality OTG devices actually BLOCK the path of electricity back to the device

All that said, the right angle connection can be a problem with my phone when it's in a case. I have a Galaxy S4 and all of my flash drives require a boost from another USB source to be attached to the micro female port.

title: Super buggy touchpad...Too much hassle for $700
text:
I've had this for a little over half a year now (I ordered it June 28, 2017) and I'm ready to make my review on this laptop. Firstly I'd like to say it's very lightweight and that really comes with its perks because before this I had a very wide screen laptop that was relatively heavy and it was a pain to carry around on a college campus with hills. However within just a month I began to notice troubles with the touch pad, where simply placing your finger on the touchpad would make the cursor jump to a new position on the screen. Most times I would simply place my finger on the touch pad and then use another finger to hit the left click. I would say about 20% of the time when my finger touches the left click button the pointer would jump to the bottom left and corner so when I click it would open up the Windows start menu. This is very frustrating and really ruins the whole point of even having a laptop touchpad...it was pretty much consistently unusable. I tried to rollback my software update, rebooting my computer and then reinstalling the latest drivers from their website, even switching to a new OS. The touch pad issue would, in fact, get worse. I searched forums for solutions to no avail.

So to end this review, if you use your laptop on a daily basis with an accompanying mouse and mouse pad, then sure this problem doesn't really concern you. It has an SSD so naturally the boot-up speeds are pretty fast because that's the whole point of having a solid-state drive. If you plan to use your laptop comfortably on a couch, on a bed, anywhere that wouldn't have the hassle of navigating with an external mouse, I would steer away from this awful buggy laptop. Nowadays I essentially use it to watch shows and do some light coding on it using an external mouse; completely disabling the touch pad. It is definitely not worth the $730 I paid in total for this.

I had an electrician years ago disable it on two nice little Panasonics I got from JC Penney, because it was a pain in the ass. Even at home, I'm already picking up the stylus and putting the record away before it has time to run out to label.

I guess belt drive or direct is a personal preference, or they wouldn't still make both, but I can't imagine why anyone would want a rubber belt that's only going to stretch out of shape over time and adversely affect the way your records sound. Direct drives hit speed almost instantaneously, maintain consistent speed more reliably over time - and you can't slip-cue with a belt drive TT at all, because when you hold the record in place, the belt drive turntable slows down or stops completely. That totally blows. Gimme a table with horsepower.

In any case, it just seems to me that the only two aspects that anyone has complained about on this turntable are both built that way for a reason. The real question mark is it's durability. A well-built TT should hold up for decades, if it's not manhandled. Crosley has a reputation for making decorative toys, rather than real high-end audio equipment - this product could be a good way for them to start turning their brand around.

The real curiosity is that this turntable is a dead ringer for the Audio Technica AT-LP120 - take a close look and compare them, they're literally IDENTICAL, as though they were pressed from the same mold. If Audio Technica isn't making them for Crosley and just slapping on a different label, they should be suing for patent infringement on their design. In other words, when you buy one of these, you may actually be getting an Audio Technica at a discount, with a Crosley sticker on it. But you didn't hear that from me.

Update: Having had the opportunity now to compare the Crosley directly to an Audio Technica, I can say conclusively they are not the same. The Crosley is more like a trainer unit for teaching young people how to care for vinyl and stereo equipment. It's not a cheap toy, OTOH the AT is noticeably superior, and (as of this writing) not that much more expensive.

title: Not Ready for Prime Time
text:
First thing after opening the box I realized that this was not a professional-grade item. One end of the arm ball joint would be loose enough to position, but the other end of the ball joint arm became frozen so it would not move. Loosening the knob more, the end that was loose became frozen and the other end loosened up. Back and forth like this the whole time. Convinced me that this item, once attached to a tripod and a monitor, would be a monstrous pain to adjust.

Moreover, I realized that I'd have to tighten the knob beyond belief to get the ball joints to hold position, without having a load on either end. I was imagining what it would be like having to hang a 7" Marshall monitor on one end, with all that leverage, if the whole thing would hold up reliably after having to move the tripod and the whole rig to reposition for the next shot.

It was frustrating just playing with it on the bench, so just imagine what you'd be fighting while a monitor was attached. I'm no longer adjusting myself to the whims and foibles of half-baked products, the so-so type, where you justify the retention on the basis of the lower price. It's the way you end up with a junk pile of gear that you fight every step of your ownership.

Some of the other offerings did mention the construction materials, but I didn't see any mention of it here. It's also available on Bee & H which has similar review ratings, not as many unfavorable as mine is. There are some others made of stainless and others made of aluminum, but many look exactly the same as this item, but branded differently. I've given up trying to figure out if they're all $19 items, but priced variously from $19 all the way up to $85. They all look exactly the same to me. So, I'm not buying any of them.

Thank goodness for Amazon's return policy. I've saved the box and the packaging, so I've sent it back in pristine condition and decided to buy a Noga for three times the price, $140. Killing me, but that's a better option than fighting this item all the way to oblivion.

title: Really not so good. Maybe even a 2-star product. For amateurs maybe 4-stars.
text:
Not so easy to rate. Let's see. Might be a 1-star product for hi ND values, and 4 stars for low ND values. Amazon service was very good so I am going with 3 stars. With low ND values (very low ones) there's no problem: not too much color cast and "shading is pretty uniform". But there's a really strange thing: overall the filter does not affect sharpness, but locally, there are lots of blurry spots on the image (not a dirty filter, not a dirty lens/sensor), like there were water drops on the lens. At high ND values, when the sun is up and strong... oh God. Unusable. Total mess. First of all, blurry spots are still there. Not talking about pixel-peeping, they will be noticeable also on a 12-Mpx sensor. Second, a big X-shaped, curved shading appears along the image (and not an easily fixable one... I'm talking about 2-3 exposure stops shadings). Color cast shows strongly but not uniformly. Top and lower opposite corners will be blueish and the other zones will be brownish. When I went outdoors to try it I had to take 4-5 times each shot rotating the filter to later make a stacked image in PS. Lost hours fixing blurry spots, color cast, and stacking images, yet some where not accepted into image banks, due to sharpness problems. Really not happy overall with the filter, already ordered another one of another brand. Amazon service was very good.

I see many 5-star ratings. Maybe these people hasn't had to use the filter on very sunny conditions, or maybe they stopped down the diafragm to f/22 to compensate and not have to get to high ND values. But for a professional, nedding to use decent f values, this is unacceptable.

title: Impressive for the Price
text:
I've only listened to a couple podcasts and some deep house (via Oliver Heldens's Soundcloud), but so far they seem to be great. Since my closed back monitors are the Audio Technica M50xs, I may be used to a more neutral/flat sound. However, these sound pretty great for the price. The build quality is top notch. It's nice that the earcups are attached to the headband with metal bits that have a really nice satin finish.

They don't isolate noise, obviously, since they're open back, but it seems like higher pitched or harsher external sounds are almost amplified in the cups. I'm typing on a mechanical keyboard while I listen to music, and I can hear the key presses pretty clearly (Cherry MX Speeds -> silver switch). The sound is good overall, and I imagine in a quiet environment they'd be great to use due to the neutral sound and less pressure in the ears. Testing the sound egress, I've found it to be mild, but you'll still want to be wary of the volume in which you're listening to your music so as not to disturb anyone relatively close (within 2 meters).

What comes in the box:
Rigid, zippered carrying case
Small canvas drawstring bag for cables and adapters
Long, braided cable (has threading on one end for 6.35mm adapter)
Shorter, braided cable with music control and microphone
Airplane connector adapter
Gold plated 3.5mm to 6.35mm adapter
Small user guide which includes an acoustic curve graph

Some things I'm curious about:
Is it actual wood? They look nice, but I question whether the wood is real, and I don't feel like dismantling them to find out.
Is it real leather? It has a bit of the synthetic smell to it, unlike real leather.
Acoustic differences based on ear cup/driver chamber shape, wood choice, etc between this model and others (e.g. SV005, SV007, etc)

Overall, I can't give a full recommendation at this point, as I'll need to use them for a longer period of time to get a full read on how they perform. However, my initial impressions are very positive. One minor nitpick is typos in the manual

title: So you want to cool your GPU easily and more cheaply than a full ...
text:
So you want to cool your GPU easily and more cheaply than a full watercooling loop? Great! This is cheaper for sure. Somewhat easier I suppose.

I bought this to cool my Titan X. The air cooled setup was sitting at 40C idle. Currently at 31C with a Corsair H60 cooler. I will post an update for temperatures under load later.

Alrighty lets get to part everyone wants to know. How easy was this to install? Fairly easy to get the HG10 N980 onto the Titan after removing the air cool block. The hard part was getting the H60 radiator to fit in a good spot in my case. Because Corsair's hoses dont bend very well. Or at all really. Also you dont want a ton of pressure on the hoses because guess what? Theyre attached to a thousand dollar video card and you dont want to bend the card. Definitely glad I didnt buy a larger radiator such as an H100i or something. The hoses just arent that long and since the hoses dont face out like if you were cooling a CPU then you get to have some fun fitting everything without breaking stuff. But its all done now. Total time for installation was about 45 minutes or so. I took my time to take pictures and such though so if you know what youre doing you could probably be done faster.

Things that you will most likely need/have to buy:
1. A fan power splitter cable x2. I got lucky and had a few of these from other builds I've done. You need one for the fan and one for the pump on whatever cooler you end up buying.
2. Small phillips screwdriver. To take off the air cooling block, install new block, ect.
3.Thermal paste. This ones up to you. Corsair does pre-coat their cooling rigs but I like to do it myself just to make sure.
4. Rubbing alcohol and Q tips. To clean off the old thermal paste on the GPU.

Things to watch out for:
1. Dont overtighten the screws holding the cooling bracket onto the video card. Good way to crack/bend the card.
2. Make sure that you reattach the plate that holds the card to the case. You definitely need the support.

Edit:
So after playing some games I have some temps finally. Playing Skyrim for an hour never got over 40C. The big one was playing Elite Dangerous at 4k. With air cool I was hitting 80C+, now with this and and H60 im getting 44C after 2 hours of gaming. Much better. Still worried about all that weight on the card though. Really really wishing that EVGA included a backplate for the Titan X. I will be buying a backplate as soon as they are back in stock for more support and better cooling.

title: Prepare to pay more than what is listed on Amazon
text:
I purchased this because I wanted better security than the consumer grade equipment provides. In short, I wanted a firewall rather than a router for my security.

To that goal the SonicWall TZ105 delivers a basic firewall. And as many others have noted here this is all about the upsell to additional features not included with the base product. Just get used to the dialogue box which reads, "Not Licensed". Furthermore there is NO SUPPORT with this product unless you pay for it. While it is common to sell support packages for continuing support, I am surprised there is no initial support available. If it is defective new-in-the-box, no one will pick up the phone to help out.

The biggest complaint I have is it only comes with 60-days of firmware updates. I get the whole 'monetize everything' concept, but I think this is too far. The problem is this is a security device. If it has a vulnerability at some point in the future, I will have no choice but to pay SonicWall / Dell money to fix something that is a defect in their product. I think this is out of place for a hardware device of this nature.

Let me put it a different way... Let's say a car manufacturer discovers a defect which can cause the car to crash catastrophically with a loss of life. They issue a recall notice to fix the problem for free. With SonicWall, if there is a security related defect it could result in the loss of data, privacy, and resources, SonicWall / Dell will charge you to fix their issue.

So one star off for being a marketing / upsell tool. A second star off for charging customers to fix product defects.

title: Great Tripod even after 7 months of hard use..12-31-15 update...
text:
**UPDATE 12-31-15**

I have used this with my Fujifilm X-S1, X10, GE X500, and Insignia Video Cameras. It has been, and fell, on concrete, mud, streams, down a slightly large hills (both land & asphalt) and tho it looks like cr@p, NOTHING has broke or became loose, and overall it is STILL a solid tripod. And this "junk ball head" has been rock solid thru out it all.

I don't care what anyone says about the Dolica brand, ALL brands have lemons, and ALL have jems. And in MY experience I have had more jems from Dolica than any other piece of camera gear I have ever owned in 50 years of shooting.

**Original**

I have been a Dolica user for years. Now I am NOT a “fan boy”, but a good deal is a good deal, and so far every piece of Dolica gear I own has been 100% functional. I have had a ST650 forever it seems, and it was getting a little wore out...so I went looking for another tripod, but this one needed to be more portable then the ST650.

It was between this one and the Amazon Basics 62inch tripod, but the Dolica won out for 2 reasons....'

1. I liked the single-lever on the ball head instead of the 2 knobs on the Amazon

2. I liked the flip release levers on the Dolica instead of the twist locks on the Amazon

Bottom line, the Dolica has been solid every time I have taken it out, easy to adjust, rock solid once setup, and light to carry. The camera locks in place & does not move, I have no problem carrying the tripod-camera around, that is how solid the plate feels. The legs are loose until you snap the locks, and then you can not budge them.

The center column, just like the ST650, when extended & locked in place really IS solid, not like rock solid, but I am not afraid to use it fully extended.....and when extended it brings the camera to eye level of my 6' 1 1/2“ frame.

The leg angle adjustments are a pain, you will NOT be adjusting angles quickly, but height adjustment is very quick. Flipping the center column to do micro photography is a slight pain, and I more than once have almost lost the bag-hook screw section. title: Comfort. Check. Wireless. Check. Sound Quality. Check. All-around MasterPiece
text:
These are brilliant headphones no doubt, and I am completely impressed with their overall quality and the noise cancellation. The other reviewers have extensively mentioned all that is to be said, so I will take a bit different approach.

I also own the previous Bose SoundLink Wireless headphones, and will compare those to this newer wireless model. For one, the new ones are around 63% heavier than both the SouldLink Wireless and the QC25 (wired, with noise cancellation) I wish Bose could have made them lighter, but you would not notice the difference if you were wearing them for a few hours at a time. It could take a toll on me if I had them on an extensive amount of time, but that is rare. The sound quality is a little upgrade to the SoundLinks, I can hear a little more base, which was well needed!

Secondly, I do not understand why Bose does not have a feature to turn off Noise cancellation when connected via Bluetooth. I mean, come on, Bose as an entire app for the iPhone where you can control/pair/name your headphones, but you cannot activate/disable noise cancellation! That would have been a very neat feature.

I like now these fold up for storage compared to the SoundLinks. Instead of only tilting the head pieces 90 degree, these do that in addition to one of the ear piece rotating to filling in the gap in the center of the headphone. I like this modification, although I am more scared more stuff can go wrong and eventually break that extra hinge.

title: Works very well, though its construction leaves a little bit to be desired.
text:
This module gets the job done well. I had the most success interfacing to it using the built-in Arduino GSM library, with RXD going to pin 3, and TXD going to pin 2. No problems with it sending and receiving SMS messages on T-Mobile's Pay-As-You-Go bring your own device plan. As of this writing, the SIMs come pre-activated, and all you need to do is whack it in the module and start sending messages.

This module runs directly on 5v supplied from an Arduino or other regulated source. This is thanks to a dropper diode on the VCC input, which simplifies the interfacing of this module vs other ones available on Amazon.

The module I received was very poorly soldered together, as if it was done quickly by hand, or that their reflow oven was not properly configured. Some of the larger caps and diodes are misaligned and seem to have poor joints. This does not have any effect on its operation, but I have gotten higher quality modules from SainSmart.

Surround sound.

Do you want to use PC headphones on your PS4?

You need this adapter. I used to use a audio/mic spitter with my PC headset BUT those always break after a couple months. Buy this USB adapter instead!

title: Impressive, and so was the service.
text:
This red one was at least $50 cheaper than the blue at the time of purchase. I can NOW attest that they are physically identical. I purchased this red one for my gf as a C-mas gift on Dec 5th. C-mas came and we took it out of the box, and it had a wheel that was pushed into its housing. I was able to pull it out, but it still was not as it should have been. There are two wheels on the back bottom, and the wheel on one side was fine. Even though the unit is supported by four rubber feet, the wheels do touch, and having one wheel not fully touching caused an imbalance, and it was harder to move around. Setup was very easy, just plug it in and turn it on. We turned it on and immediately heard a loud persistent buzzing noise. This noise was present no matter the input we chose. Loud enough to be heard about 20 feet away, around the corner, in another room. The buzz did not increase or decrease with any adjustments to volume. We also tried plugging it in to different outlets- though in hindsight it did not occur to me to make sure I was on a different circuit. (Duh.) Anyway, we got down to some music. The built in FM tuner worked well, so did the Bluetooth, and anything else we plugged into it. We didn't notice the buzz through the music playing, though at lower volumes we realized it was still there. Asking the Amazon community here rewarded me with two answers- 1 that the buzz should not be there at all, and another who stated he also had the buzz. The amount of inputs and modifications and TWO equalizers, plus your standard treble/bass controls.....WOW. I am not so handy at the EQ, but this thing gets LOUD!! We could not even turn it up halfway. My cats were running for cover at 1/8 of the knob. We were both really impressed with the unit, and I resolved to see if I could go about getting a replacement wheel and housing for the broken one, plus I wanted to see what the seller said about the buzzing. I emailed the seller, mentioned that it WAS a C-mas gift, and was surprised when Kate from Galactics returned my email a scant 5 mins later! She said they were not able to offer replacement parts, and that I had had a 14 day window to make a freight damage claim, as per Amazon and FedEx policies. It had been 21 days since delivery date, so I WAS overdue. Kate asked me to take photos of the damaged wheel/housing, AND the box it was shipped in, and email her those and she would see what she could do. Wow..that was nice, though I didn't have high hopes even though the damage was obvious. I thanked her and politely mentioned that it was a C-mas gift that I didn't wanna open before C-mas and that usually sellers have some sort of extended policy during the holiday season. I then took the photos and emailed them to her. A couple more emails back and forth, confirming pictures received, etc.... I felt as though Kate from Galactics was there the whole time. In less than an hour, she was telling me the damage claim was accepted and that I would be offered a full refund, and that FedEx would be there to pick up the damaged unit within the next two days! I was really expecting this to be a hassle, and I cannot thank Kate and Galactics enough for the way this was handled. Truly excellent service to that point- and it got better. We really did not wanna lose this unit, it really REALLY is awesome....I think gf wudda been unhappy if we did not get it replaced (I really just wanted a new wheel assembly) and I heard from Kate that other customers were really fond of theirs too. After more emails with Kate over the next week, we decided to try the Blue version instead. That one had more written reviews on Amazon, and I assured Kate that I would not have a problem paying any cost difference. In my dealings with Kate and Galactics, I never had the feeling that I was forgotten about, or pushed to the side. Kate informed me that a new batch of Blue(s) was being shipped in soon, and that mine would ship out soon after. Excellent! I received my blue speaker a few days ago, and it was intact. EXACTLY the same as the red (no fan in the back of either speaker- and it's not supposed to have one). There WAS however a buzzing noise, but nowhere near as loud as the damaged red one, and it was quickly forgotten about. Just as loud and awesome as the red one. Oh, the flashing LED lights can be turned off, but note that they do not flash much or brightly at low volume. The higher the volume, the bigger/brighter the light show. Also there is a switch on the back for 220 or 240 volts, though there is only one provided (removable) plug. Hmm...I always thought it was 210 or 220......?
I saw another reviewer (for the blue model) had provided pictures of how he had linked two of these together- so it IS possible. I believe he used a mixer or some other dj equipment. Wow..I can only imagine...
Funny thing is, this was purchased because gf wasn't completely happy with all the sub $100 little Bluetooth speakers/boomboxes we were trying. Neither was I. It was time to get real. I got it for her to put in the basement for her morning workout sessions. But I just don't know now. Might not leave the living room. Do I have to buy something not as good to justify putting it in the basement? Haha.
Bottom line here: 5 Star review. We MIGHT have just kept it anyway with the broken wheel and persistent buzz. What does that tell you about the awesomeness of the speaker??
By the way, Kate said not to worry about any price difference- it was on them. Gotta love her. There was nothing done wrong by the seller, and they went out of their way to make things right for me, all the while making me feel special. Thanks again Kate. I will be looking to buy from Galactics again after this experience, even if the cost is a little higher. Highest recommendations and praise to Kate and Galactics. THANK YOU!!

title: Awesome display and one cable to rule them all!
text:
We bought 5 of these for our office and LOVE them. Everything just works as advertised, including:
* Beautiful 4k display. Deep blacks, great color saturation, low latency.
* USB Type-C connectivity bidirectionally charging and displaying: Using the included USB Type-C cable, we're using three different new Mac and PC laptop models and all can charge *from* the monitor *and* send 4k video *to* the monitor *and* use the monitor's USB-A ports for low-power USB devices. Our laptops models are:
** Late-2016 MacBook Pro 13"
** Late-2016 MacBook Pro 15"
** Early-2017 HP Spectre x360 15"
* Even though the 15" laptops come with larger 87w and 90w USB Type-C power supplies, they still charge just fine (albeit slower) off the monitor's 60w output. Since we're at our desks much of the day, slower charging is just fine and allows us to keep our factory power supplies at home, saving $100/each on buying additional power adapters per laptop.
* We each have Microsoft Sculpt wireless keyboards and Logitech wireless mice, and the two nano wireless USB transmitters plug simply into the back of the monitor since it's a USB hub.
** Note that with the 15" laptops, the remaining available power (there's only 60w total to go around) to the USB hub ports on the monitor is *very* low. For example, we can run a Microsoft nano USB wireless transmitter for the keyboard, and usually a Logitech nano USB wireless transmitter for the mouse, but *cannot* run a higher-end Logitech Unifying receiver (uses more power apparently than the non-Unifying nano receiver) and if you try to charge a device from one of the two USB hub ports simultaneously with the other port used by the Microsoft nano USB wireless transmitter, the transmitter will keep cutting out and you'll have a frustrating keyboard day. There's just only so much power to go around, this isn't the monitor's fault.
** This doesn't seem to be a problem with the 13" laptops because their USB Type-C power requirements are lower so the 60w from the monitor goes further.

All this said, we have full desk setups now with absolutely minimal cabling:
1) Power to monitor.
2) USB Type-C from monitor to laptop.
3) Wireless input peripherals with close-proximity transceivers (back of the monitor).

Highly recommend this awesome monitor.

The picture quality is good, but not great for online streaming content. I was warry of Android TV reliability on Sony TVs, based on initial user reviews, but Android TV has been quite stable for me in the past 6 months. The main reasons I got this TV over other TVs was the native Smart interface. I wanted to have the luxury of using one remote to turn on the TV and navigate the TV interface right away. If there was a TV in the same price range that had a relatively superior interface (like Roky, arguably) I would have gone for that. But the current TV's with Roku built-in are low-end. Other reason to choose Sony's implementation of Android TV was availability of Amazon Video, which is a big deal, since other Android TVs and also Apple TV don't offer. I can say Amazon Video compatibility and Google Cast are the main advantages Sony's current TV interface has over other TV interfaces. Integration with PlayStation Now and dual shock is another plus.

Cons:
1). Sony TV Recommended Apps feature on the second row of interface ruins the Android TV experience completely. It means you have to take up to 3-4 more steps in order to launch your intended TV app. Terrible. Almost kills all the Android TV other positives.
2). Not able to connect Bluetooth headphones, contrary to what was advertised.
3). Miracast doesn't work with Windows decices, contrary to what was advertised.
4). Dual shock game controllers can either be connected to Android TV/Play station Now or PlayStation device itself. Would have been great if it could be able to seamlessly connect to both at the sametime.
4). PlayStation Now service is too expensive.
5). Playststion Vue service is not available on Sony Android TV platform as we speak. Could be a game changer for recommending Sony TVs over competition, when if becomes available.

title: First Windows, then 12 years with a Mac, and now, finally...happiness!
text:
I'm a retired geek and first used Windows (from the day it first released) and for the past 12 years, I've used all Apple products. Over the past year, I've become somewhat disenchanted with Apple regarding their computers, the current problems they have with the MacBook Pro, and the fact that an iMac refresh is long overdue. Apple derives about 85% of its revenue from all their products EXCEPT computers...so their heart really hasn't been in it. They're a great company, but not as great as they once were.

I would never go back to Windows, yet I knew I couldn't stay with Apple, so that left Chrome OS. I looked at all the best Chromebooks and the only one that truly impressed me was the Google Pixelbook. I've always used Gmail (since its first beta) and I have always had one foot in the Google ecosphere with Gmail, Drive, and Google Photos already, so making the move seemed logical.

Three weeks into a complete switch, I feel I made the right decision and also chose the right device. The Pixelbook is every bit as wonderfully made as my eight-month-old MacBook Pro was (I already sold it). The display is amazing, the keyboard FAR BETTER than the MacBook Pro, and in all regards, I am completely happy with the Pixelbook.

I still have my iPhone X, but when the Pixel 3 XL releases this fall, I'll be trading in the iPhone. The iPhone X is a great phone, but after playing around extensively with the Pixel 2 XL I'm convinced there are many things it does better. If you're on the fence about purchasing the Pixelbook...go ahead and try it. If you don't like it you can always return it...but I'm betting you won't!

title: Great Wireless Headphones
text:
Samsung has another winner with the Gear Icon X wireless headphones. The design is very nice; the case is small enough to easily carry and I love that it has its own battery that will charge buds in between full plug-in charges. The fit is very comfortable and is easily adjustable with the different sizes of 'pads' and 'wingtips' and those wingtips really help them stay in place. The sound quality is excellent, too; I'm really impressed by how these excel at playing all types of music. It took me a few tries to figure out how to swipe up and down on the buds to control the volume without accidentally tapping (which toggles between play and pause), but now it feels very natural.

Due to an injury, I haven't yet been able to use the fitness-oriented features for anything other than walks but I like the coaching option so far. And, it can be disabled for those times when I don't want or need the guidance. I tend to carry my phone with me everywhere but I do like the ability to store music directly on the buds; this and the fact that the buds will store my workout information to sync with the Samsung Health app later mean I can use them without my phone if I want. One of my favorite features is Ambient Sound; this uses a second microphone on the top of each bud to pick up and then play outside sounds. It's really useful when listening to music on walks in busy areas or when listening at work, for example, and I expect it will come in very handy when cycling so that I can hear surrounding traffic.

Pros:
-The fit; they stay snugly in my ears but are still very comfortable
-The sound quality is great for all types of music
-The fitness features (coaching and activity tracking)
-The carrying case doubles as a backup charger
-The Ambient Sound feature is great for convenience and safety
-The touch controls

Cons:
-The touch controls can be a little tricky to figure out at first
-The price is a little steep

title: Great pocket sized tablet with an impressive CPU
text:
In my line of work I have used Android tablets before to test websites and apps, but this is the first one I have ever owned. I got to finally go beyond the browser and app store.

// FEEL
The tablet is a good size, not too heavy, and they tapered the back of the case (near the edges) to make holding it more pleasant and comfortable.It really is a nice touch for when you are holding the tablet for long periods.

The case is a smooth plastic, but doesn't feel like it would slip out of your hands. I feel I have no need for a rubber/silicone case to help prevent it from slipping out of my hands.

// PERFORMANCE
The CPU is impressive for this pricepoint! The ARM A33 Cortex-A7 1.5GHZ Quad-Core is more powerful than my iPad 2's CPU (ARM 1GHZ dual core). The browser loads websites quickly, loads and plays music very quickly, and I never ran into and issue with most popular apps loading and running well.

// BATTERY
My unit came with 0% charge, so I had to charge it up in order to turn it on. I've played music, browsed websites, used a handful of apps, downloaded 10MB files, and the battery seems to hold up well. The claimed 4 hour battery life seems a good average for normal usage.

// SCREEN
The screen resolution of 1024x600 is good (I can't seem to find the pixel density listed anywhere.) It's the brightness and the fact that colors change if you view it from an angle that I am not a fan of. Out of the box the screen was really bright, so I had to turn it down. When I moved back to the iPhone and iPad, I noticed the colors of the Irulu are just okay, bordering on washed out. When viewing through the camera it looks like you are seeing the world through a dirty/misty window.

The response to taps is good, but noticed that sometimes I have to tap twice or extra hard.

I did notice that when you view the home screen in portrait mode, the Irulu circle is a bit oblong, but more of a true circle when in landscape mode. Google "circle" and turn the table around and see for yourself: the portrait mode seems to stretch the screen vertically a tiny bit, but enough to make circles a little oblong. Nothing drastic, and most people won't notice.

// MUSIC
Music sounds great. Again, for the pricepoint and the fact it is using the onboard audio processing, it sounds almost as good as any smartphone out there.

// CAMERA and PICTURES
The camera is good enough. It's not even comparable to the iPhone 6 or Galaxy cameras. But, again, for this pricepoint the camera works well and takes pictures. In situations where the light is medium to low, the camera does not take good pictures, and they tend to turn of fuzzy. I do not plan on using this as a camera, so I am not worried.

// WIFI
I did have some trouble connecting to the wifi at home and work. I had to enter it twice and turn the wifi off/on to get it to connect. Once it finally connected, the device connects to the wifi really fast each time I turn it on or move from office to home and back.

// GREAT FOR...
This tablet is great for:
— travel
— kids
— testing websites and apps on an Android
— event booths
— kiosks/checkins
— loner tablets for hospitality/concierge

I am not reducing any stars because where it comes up short (camera) I am not really concerned with since I am not going to use the camera. The screen is good enough, but not iPad level. Again, the performance is impressive for the price, which more than makes up for any shortcomings.

I received a free sample of this product to evaluate and provide an unbiased review.

title: Great for the Price
text:
I bought this just a week ago because I just needed an estimate of my yardage to the greens. For that purpose it is a great buy at less than $50. It is small and lightweight, has a nice ring to attach to my golf cart or it can unobtrusively fit in my pocket. I found the yardage to be fairly accurate. Recognize that 4-5 yards difference between my $50 device and my golf buddy's $190 laser scope is irrelevant to us bogey golfers.
However the Izzo Sport is not without a few shortcomings for me. First, the fully charged battery only lasted 3.5 hours. It could be because it is new and needs to be charged and recharged a few more times to increase battery capacity; it could be because I frequently push the buttons and perhaps using extra juice on the white background screen. We will see.
My chief issue is that one must physically tap the button to move the device from one hole to the next. I'm in my mid-60's so my eyes don't do so well with small print. I don't always hit this button because I'm caught in the moment with a great putt or some other distraction. While I'm walking or riding down the next fairway I have a hard time seeing the little number on the bottom left of the screen that tells me what hole the GPS is registering. So sometimes it gives me to the distance to the hole I'm on and sometimes the one I just left. Yeah, my bad. But, if you have young eyes and are on a budget, this is a great deal.
I saw some reviews that complained about this device requiring a reset of some kind from spot to spot on the way to a green. I didn't have any problem whatsoever. I saw a comment from Izzo that the software was updated on all these devices sold after May of 2015.

title: Worked for less than 24 hours. EDIT: device seems to have recovered.
text:
Second edit: dropped down to 3 stars since the remote isn't rechargeable for some reason, takes really weird batteries, and I can't use a universal remote with it since, for some crazy reason, it doesn't have an IR receiver that both the previous generation and the pro version have. IR receivers cost like $1 wholesale, no idea why they would remove it specifically for this version, except as a money grab to try to get you to spend more on the Pro version. I wish I'd gone with a different media player.

EDIT: After watching the device stuck on a black screen after boot for about 5 minutes, I left the room to Google how to troubleshoot it. When I went back 30 minutes later, it was running and on the Chromecast screensaver. It seems to be working for now - perhaps the black screen was doing some sort of recovery process in the background? I'll keep an eye on it. Aside from this issue and difficulty finding how to fastboot it, the device has worked very well. I've updated my review to 3 stars, will bump it up higher if things continue to go well.

When it arrived, things seemed mostly good. During the setup process, it prompted me to update the controller firmware. I accepted, but the update failed. I tried to do the update again, but it wouldn't allow me to. The controller seemed to work so I kept using it. Got Netflix and PLEX set up, everything seemed good so far.

But then this morning when I tried to wake it up, it popped up a warning saying that the Shield Controller Service had crashed and asked me to restart it. That wasn't possible since the controller was no longer working, so I unplugged it and plugged it back in. Now all I get is a black screen, the device won't start any longer.

So I decided to do a factory reset and try again. I'm a programmer so I don't mind getting into the bootloaders and such if I have to, but all of the instructions online are for the 2015 version of the device and don't work with the new 2017 version - they require you to press the NVidia Shield button on top of the device, but the 2017 device has no buttons on it at all.

So the device is now unusable and all of the instructions to try to recover it don't work on this version of the device because of the insane decision to remove its only button. I'd exchange it, but I don' think I want this version of the Shield - not having a button to hard reset a device seems asinine given that it can be bricked just through normal use.

title: The Perfect Leather Case for the Gold iPad Pro???
text:
This is probably the perfect case for the larger 12.9" iPad Pro, if you're looking for GENUINE leather that looks good with the Gold version of the iPad. Fit and finish are both excellent. The case smells good too, although I wish it smelled a little MORE. :-)

I had a version of this case for a little over a year on my smaller 9.7" Air 2 before upgrading to the 12.9" iPad Pro. The case wears nicely and actually looks better and better over time with handling and use. I use the cover's folded up stand feature allot in the kitchen when cooking. I was afraid that the larger iPad would have issues with this, but it works perfectly and is as stable as it was on my 9.7".

All cutouts for the four speakers, buttons, headphone jack and charging port are cut accurately. The camera cutout is SLIGHTLY off center, but not enough to cause issues.

Now for the downside; The STUPID gold brand-badge on the lower right front cover. This badge is metal and arc shaped, so it's raised and not flush with the cover. Over time, when the cover is flipped open and held, this badge is going to wear an uneven hole/dent in the back of the case. The 9.7" version of this case does not have this badge.

Overall, though, I'm happy with the case and it looks stunning, adds very little thickness and is easy to hold. Given the few available choices for GENUINE leather cases, this is certainly the best option.

title: so good. After trying a couple of other really inexpensive ...
text:
So far, so good. After trying a couple of other really inexpensive (aka "cheap") Chinese-made cameras, I thought I'd go upmarket just a bit for another. Although this one is also of course Chinese made, the reviews were mostly OK and I bought it. It arrived quickly as it was available with Prime. Before it did, I received an Amazon Marketplace email update reminding me that it required a Class 4 Micro SD card as one isn't included. It also had a copy of the instruction manual included... which was actually fairly well done. So I had a better feeling about the camera before it even arrived.

I plugged it in to the 12v plug in my car after I received the camera, and it was much easier to figure out and get setup than the less expensive junk models I'd purchased previously. The image quality is much better than the earlier cameras, too. The extended-length power cord is apparently better quality too, and still is long enough to reach from mounting behind the rear view mirror, along the roof liner, and then under the dash to my 12v plug in the center console. My only complaint is that the suction pad seems to lose it's grip, as I've had to dig around on the floor to find the camera a few times after coming back to a parked car, and once it did that while driving. I think I have it figured out, and hopefully that problem will go away.

The other issue that I've seen other reviews mention I've experienced as well, in that the camera slips off the mount while driving. Seems to be missing something there. But as at least one other reviewer asked for a replacement mount and it didn't improve things, I opted to just tape in to the mount with a small wrap of black electrical tape. Just means I have to disconnect the suction cup and put the whole camera away if protecting it from the heat. OK solution for my needs. The suction cup and slipping off the mount issues are my only problems with this camera.

I've been happy with the quality of the video I've taken over the past few days, which while not great isn't terrible by any means. The audio recording is actually really good on the camera, something the cheaper cameras I'd had couldn't handle at all.

My review may be updated if it also dies a sudden death, but for now 4 stars seems appropriate to me, especially for the price versus the even cheaper ones I'd tried earlier.

title: ZERO STARS POS do not buy !!!
text:
Right out of the box there was trouble. When trying to pair the watch with my phone I got an error message that my "device" was not compatible. A call to tech support (available 8 to 6 CST at 800 800-1020) revealed that while my phone (Samsung Note II) was on the compatibility list, my version of the Android OS was not new enough. Installing the latest version fixed the problem. So be warned, to pair the watch to your phone make sure that your Android OS is 4.3 or later. However, after pairing and connecting the watch to the Garmin Connect App I went too far away from the phone, lost the Bluetooth connection, and it would not reconnect. A second call to Tech support revealed that the problem is in either the watch, the phone, or Bluetooth technology. To identify which device is at fault I'll have to pair it with another phone, go out of range to lose the connection and see if it will reconnect. If it reconnects then the problem is with my phone. If not then the problem is with the watch. If it's the watch they will send me a replacement. If it's my phone I guess I'm SOL. So as of now I have a $300 "smart" watch on which the "smart" (i.e. Bluetooth) features are disabled.

Stay tuned I will be updating on the eventual outcome of the connectivity problem as well as the performance of the fitness tracking features.

10:29pm 4/2/15 - Turns out it's a problem on my Note II. I paired the watch with my wife's phone (Galaxy S), and it worked fine. The weather data and notifications showed up on the watch face. I walked out of range of the Bluetooth. When I returned the watch promptly reconnected to my wife's phone.

T-Mobile tech support told me I'll have to do a master reset to "try" to fix the Bluetooth function on my phone (full backup of apps and data - hard reset - then restore). This is turning out to be quite a project.

I'm raising my rating to 4 stars because, my problem is not the fault of the watch. However I can't give 5 stars because, other than the watch face, the notification and setting screens are very difficult (though not impossible) to read.

Tomorrow I'll take it for a run and see how the GPS, HR and Pace tracking work.

4/4/15 - I went for a run. The GPS and HR features worked fine. Using Garmin Express is effective and sends information to my calorie counting app it just does not do it in real-time the way it would if my Bluetooth would work properly.

Doing the master reset on my phone took several hours and was about as much fun as a root canal. Most of the apps and data were restored but, there were still a lot of things to do to get the phone back to its previous state. AND, after all the hassle of doing the reset the watch and phone would initially pair but STILL not reconnect. T-Mobile is sending me a replacement phone which means more backing up and restoring.

4/8/15 AFTER REPLACING THE PHONE (reinstalling and reconfiguring all my apps which took hours) the watch paired with my phone. HOWEVER, when I walked out of range, and returned THE WATCH WOULD STILL NOT RECONNECT WITH THE PHONE.

I'm keeping the watch (BUT LOWERING MY RATING TO ONE STAR to reflect my level of satisfaction with the whole experience) because the other features (GPS, HR monitoring, activity and sleep tracking) are satisfactory. Using the charging cradle and Connect Express to upload my data is not too big of a hassle. It's just not ALL of what I paid for.

4/8/15 I called to Garmin Tech support to report the failure to reconnect. After a few minutes conferring with the "mobile support specialist" the tech agent came back to say that because of how Samsung implemented Bluetooth on the Note 2 the watch will pair but not reconnect after being out of range. After hanging up I realized that I should have asked "WHY THEN IS THE NOTE 2 LISTED ON THE GARMIN WEBSITE AS A COMPATIBLE DEVICE?!?!?!"

04/16/15 - Firmware update to 2.7 but still cannot reconnect to Bluetooth. I use the charging cradle and Express Connect to upload my date and keep the watch battery at 100% charge. The watch provides very accurate and interesting feedback about the porperties of my running. To track strength training I use the indoor walking app to record time,, heart rate, and calories without turning on GPS. After exercising, I upload the date to Garmin Connect and then sync to MyFitnessPal to track net calories. Before bed I upload my steps and put the watch into sleep mode. In the morning I upload my sleep data. All in all it's not a bad experience but, it's still does not work as advertised. Reading the Garmin forum I found that many people are having pairing and connection problems with many different models and brands of phones.

7/23/15 - After firmware update to 3.0, the Bluetooth connection finally started working BUT, NOW IT WILL NOT CHARGE OR CONNECT TO MY COMPUTER. Also, I found out the hard way that the heart rate monitor is not water proof. This is not mentioned in the documentation. And after about two weeks the replacement HR (that I bought) stopped working - probably not sweat proof either.

title: A very small, very nice USB hub for microUSB use
text: This is a simple 4-port USB hub with a microUSB connector.  It is designed for use with computers and operating systems (most modern ones) that support the OTG capability, which essentially allows the use of nearly any USB peripheral with your computer.  The hub is quite small, about 7/8 in. wide x 5/8 in. high x 2.5 in. long--small enough to easily get lost in your luggage :)  Its cable is only 4 in long from the hub enclosure to the connector strain relief.  While intended, and priced, for Raspberry Pi users, I bought it for an inexpensive "Ematic" Windows 10 tablet, with which it performs perfectly.  In my opinion as a product-making electronics/computer engineer, it is well-designed, with mechanically-solid strain reliefs at both ends of its cable, ample room for all four USB devices, a nicely-finished and reasonably-strong plastic case, and no loose parts.  As others have pointed out, the microUSB connector will not provide anything like full power (500 mA for each USB connector).  Flash drives work fine.  It would be hard to do much better than LoveRPi has done with this hub; if this is what you want, buy it.

text:
Highly recommended. If you follow the instructions your TV will be safely on the wall in no time. I used 2 of these, one for a 55" and one for a 42". The only drawback is the tilting of the TV. For heavier TVs, you will probably need to set the tilt to what you want it to be BEFORE actually hanging the TV. Once the TV is on the wall, the screws for the tilt cannot be reached (they are on the inside of the mount). Other than that, I found these very easy to use. Be sure to either put the bolts into wood studs or to use the anchors included in the package.

A few nice touches with this set: 10 foot high quality HDMI cord included (probably $5-$10 if purchased separately), mini level (you would probably want to get a larger one that works better but still nice to get a freebie), a microfiber cloth to clean up fingerprints from hanging the TV, and velcro straps to bunch wires together if you are trying to keep things neat.

Overall I think this is a tough deal to beat.

I have used this for 3 more tvs since writing my original review. Still swear by this wall mount. After installing one of them, you will be able to fly through any additional mountings. By far the easiest installation of a wall mount that I have experienced. I looked for one in a store when picking up my TV and it was almost triple the price! And you would have to buy the HDMI cord separately. I still think this is the best deal around for a tv wall mount.

title: Very difficult to insert wires
text: I hoped the pass through style of this connector would make it easier to install.  I was wrong.  The CAT6 TPS signal conductors were very difficult to push through the connector due due to the slightly thicker wire insulation of the CAT6 signal wires.  In general, I pushed just enough wire through the connector that I could then grab it with a pliars and pull it the rest of the way through...and I bought the special crimp/cut tool which added salt to the wound.  Tricks to make it work include very clean and straight cut on ends of wires using scissors or tin snips, wires perfectly straight and tightly side by side when inserting, push firmly, slowly and wiggle the connector slowly side to side to walk the wires through the holes.  We also tried the 3 piece RJ45 connector with the alignment block.  The holes for the conductor wires were much larger and very easy to push the wires through.  Watch You Tube videos before doing either.

text:
I got the Teorder HDMI unit to replace a very old model that was very large and ran hot, hot. The Teorder unit is about half size of my cellphone, but little thicker.

Took me just a few minutes to hook up (took me longer to remove the old bulky unit) and worked without having to do anything else. True plug and play device and I have much better resolution. My use is for interfacing to a "headless" audio/video home entertainment setup. Just in case, "headless" means: I do not use the old laptop keyboard, use a built-in point and click interface within Plex ([...]) over my local network.

The Teorder unit's HDMI port is plugged into the old laptop and the RCA ports are hooked to my 5GHz video transmitter (SainSonic SS-530). This allows me to watch videos and listen to music in outside shop / patio area with all the wires:) Basically I can watch anywhere within 500ft of my entertainment center.

For the price point and fact powers itself from laptop HDMI port cannot find one single thing bad to say. Works like it should and very little heat be produced. Full five stars from me. I did receive this unit at discount in exchange for unbiased review.

title: Essential Accessory for Every iPhone Video Shooter
text:
If you like to make video with a cell phone, this is one of the two coolest accessories you can possibly buy. The second would be a [[ASIN:B00EO4A7L0 Rode smartLav+ Lavalier Microphone for iPhone and Smartphones]] external microphone. This little inexpensive accessory from Joby produces results like a professional fluid head tripod, a thousand dollar look. The flexible tripod legs will adapt to almost any surface, whether it is a level table top, an irregular surface like a rock, or the legs can even be wrapped around small objects like a handrail, tree limb, or practically anything that is not too large to be grasped by hand.

Joby GorillaPods have been around the photography world for many years. What makes this particular GorillaPod standout from all the others, however, the thing that makes it a "Video Tripod" is the special pan and tilt head. While other GorillaPods are great for still cameras, this one has a special head made specially for video shooters that allows super smooth camera moves, the equivalent of turning your head or looking up or down. Combined with the incredible portability of the GorillaPod, this makes this device a real shot-getter. Not only is this good for holding your camera steady, if you fold all the GorillaPod legs together, they also make a sweet handle to go mobile with your cell phone or point and shoot with no fear of dropping the camera.

This bundle includes a separate Joby accessory, the GripTight. Basically, the GripTight is a simple spring loaded jaw with rubber teeth that will grip almost any cell phone and attach it to the GorillaPod Video Tripod. You could buy these two devices separately - the ones in the bundle are exactly the same as the products Joby sells separately, and they can both be used independently of each other. In other words, if you have a point and shoot camera with a conventional 1/4-20 tripod thread, it will fit on this GorillaPod. And if you have just about any iPhone or even the oversized iPhone 6 Plus, the GripTight will hold the iPhone and allow it to be mounted on any normal tripod. 1/4-20 "quarter-twenty" tripod heads have been standards forever, at least since the 1950s and probably before, so the GripTight is perfect to secure a cell phone to almost any camera mount ever invented.

This device is not specific to iPhone, though it works perfectly with every iPhone ever made. Anything larger than an Apple iPhone 6 Plus would be a problem because the jaw of the GripTight will only open wide enough for the iPhone 6 Plus. In fact, I had to remove my iPhone 6 Plus from a thin case. I've seen a few super large Samsung Galaxy smartphones that are probably too big for the GripTight. Not many people I know have a phone that big, but if you do, check Joby's published specs to see if it will fit the GripTight.

These two products from Joby are a terrific bundle, and they also fold down to a very tiny size, perfect for transport in a pocket, with no loose pieces. I have other cell phone adapters for tripods, and this is by far the best design. Even with the GripTight installed on the GorillaPod, you can fold everything down, including the tripod legs, the pan handle, and the GripTight, into a very compact package that is so small, it can fit inside a paper towel tube, and take up only about half the tube. Plus, this entire combo weights less than my iPhone 6 Plus, making this an ideal little accessory for anyone who wants to product really high quality video with an iPhone.

This particular GorillaPod also features magnets inside the three blue rubberized balls at the end of each tripod leg. These magnets are not strong enough to secure the tripod and a camera to the hood of a moving vehicle, but they do add welcome stability to keep the legs where you want them anytime you can setup the tripod on metal surfaces that are magnetically attractive.

This is purchase is actually my second Joby GorillaPod Video Tripod. This is such a terrific little product, so inexpensive, and so perfect for the intended application of making your small format video professionally stable. It is perfect for travel, very unobtrusive, and tiny enough to easily fit in almost any pocket or purse. You can leave it in you car's glovebox to have ready at all times. And it is perfect for parents - sure to be on my Christmas list for anyone shooting baby pictures. Highly recommended!
