title: Waterproof!
text: I bought these on a Prime Day special to take to South Padre Island to use for close up viewing of gulls and shorebirds on the beach and for viewing from beach to wave surface. My husband and I are fairly serious birders and own numerous pairs of slightly higher end and stronger magnification binoculars and spotting scopes. I really didn't consider these to be super legit optics, just an affordable backup pair for the beach. We had spent half an hour or so hanging out, making friends with seagulls, taking cell phone pictures. The longer I used these little binos, the more I liked them-they felt nice in the hand (love their rubberized coating!), had great edge to edge image quality, small but substantial. My (type 1 diabetic) husband seemed happy, sitting on his beach chair at the edge of the surf, dozing on and off, and enjoying the scene. But, as the low waves surrounded him, his beach chair sank deeper and deeper into the sand and I realized he was doing nothing to extricate himself. It was then I knew his blood sugar had tanked and he was already unresponsive. I had to get him up onto his feet and out of the water rickticky, pull his beach chair out of the sand, gather up all our stuff, and find him something to eat ASAP, or call 911. In the melee, I dropped the binoculars into the edge of the surf, and by the time I could grab them they (as well as my husband and I) were completely coated with sand and dripping wet. I shook the binoculars off but I had more important things to worry about, pulling my husband out of his sinkhole and getting a grip on the load of gear including both of our cellphones, the heavy beach chairs, and wet towels I would have to carry. Luckily, a woman nearby came to our rescue and helped me get him up and heading for the stairs and shower at the beach exit. Her friend gave him some crackers and, to my amazement, he came to enough to move out of the danger zone. When we reached the shower I haphazardly rinsed off the binos along with everything else. I figured they were ruined forever. I got him some food and glucose, and to this day he doesn't remember anything at all, like it never even happened. The same is true of these binoculars! As soon as they dried and I brushed the rest of the sand off of them, they were as good as new-no fog, no messed up focus wheel or gears, no scratched lenses. Even though I would have sacrificed them to my husband's medical emergency, I believe they are a great little pair of sturdy, useful, WATERPROOF, binoculars. 5 stars, easily!

title: Works GREAT - But Loud

title: This Unit Has Its Own Mind About the Order It Will Play Your Songs
text:
If I had it to do over again, I wouldn't buy this unit. Here's why:

It will not play your songs in the order you recorded them. For example, if you create a playlist on Windows Media player (on your computer), it will save and, play them in the order you want. Don't like where a particular song is on your list and you can move it to another location and re-save the playlist.

With this unit, you burn a cd from Windows Media Player (WMP) and the songs are played in a random way that I haven't found a way to change. The unit will also play music from a thumb-disk but again, the songs are played randomly. I've tried renaming the songs (i.e., 01 Deeper Well, 02 Peaceful Easy Feeling, 03 New Kid in Town, etc.) to try to trick the unit into playing the songs in the order I want but, it just doesn't work. This unit seems to have it's own individual memory and is going to play your songs in the order it wants to.

The music quality on the unit is fine. The price is fine. I like that you can also use a thumb-drive with the unit. But if you're looking for a unit that will play your music in the order YOU want, don't buy it.

title: Day One Review - ONE YEAR UPDATE
text:
I've been a user of Bose earbuds for a very long time (http://www.amazon.com/Bose-SoundTrue-In-Ear-Headphones-Black/dp/B00M5A7L14/ref=sr_1_1?s=audio-video-accessories&ie=UTF8&qid=1428323605&sr=1-1&keywords=bose+earbuds). And loved the quality of sound from such little buds while I worked out - the wing tips made them great for vigorous exercise and wouldn't fall out of my head like others.

But I was willing to take a slight (very slight) hit in quality to go bluetooth and ditch the wires. I'm so glad I bought this pair, they're top of the line right now as far as user reviews and reliability. The quality of sound is not as compromised as older models of bluetooth earbuds and the addition of winged tips make them just as secure as my old Bose. Pairing with my Android device was super easy and it's easily recognized as soon as I turn the headphones on.

My one complaint (which is more one of vanity then quality) is the fact that the monitors stick out more then I thought they would based on the pictures included here. This is a small complaint as sound and call quality are not compromised for the sake of small buds. Real-life usage of these headphones proves that they are easy to use and aren't going to quit randomly on you like a cheaper set might.

ONE YEAR UPDATE:

Almost daily use with these in the office and at the gym - these are amazing. All of my original compliments still stand and then some. I wear these around my neck when in the car so I can take calls and they fell out when I was coming home. I was busy and didn't think about it, but I left them outside... on the ground... overnight... while raining. I found them this morning and was heartbroken, thinking I'd have to buy another pair, but they were dry so I figured I'd see if there was any salvaging them even with limited functionality. I let them charge and they took a full charge and have been using them with all normal functionality all day. These are fantastic and I would recommend them to anyone.

Kind of annoying and it's either the way my Vizio tv sends the signal out or, Nakamichi needs to do some more firmware updates. It doesn't seem to like netflix on my apple tv much. When you pause the program and then restart only the surround speakers and subwoofer is working, you have to hit the volume for the sound bar to start again. So, apart from the few hiccups it's still a great product for the cost.

As a edit to this previous review I'm now confident giving this system a five star review! The CEO himself took interest in the issues I had with his companies product! What? That is practically unheard of in this day and age. He took care of my issues with this system personally and remedied them. I have received a newer updated remote, free of charge, that works much better than the original packaged remote. title: My new Fire HD 10...it's No.1!

I got it early yesterday and spent a lot of the day getting it set up, making adjustments to the menus, downloading games, books and apps and all I have to say is; Most, if not all of the people giving low-star reviews evidently just didn't know what they were doing. I didn't have problem one with anything on this tablet. I felt like the OS was quite intuitive and highly organized. Can't really imagine why anyone didn't understand it or got lost with it. I suppose that if the only thing you had ever operated was a Fire tablet with the older OS and didn't understand the Windows OS, you may have a few learning curve issues.
All of my books were there, all of my games I'd collected and my Apps, all I had to do was download what I wanted to the Tablet, very simple and very convenient. The HD display is very nice, shows absolutely no sort of pixelation as some have complained about. The response time of this tablet is exceptional and the touch screen is right on the money. I opted against a screen protector for now as that never did anything for my last tablet. These screens are extremely durable, I have a great protection case and take very good care of my things.
My bottom line is, I love my new Fire HD 10 and think it is an exceptional bargain as has been my experience with previous Fire tablets. Thus far, not a single problem and I have a hard time putting it away. I ordered the 32GB, had a 128GB mini SD to put in it I already had from another purchase that didn't work out and opted to NOT have ads remove from the lock screen. That just isn't a big deal for me. Now, with the added bonus of the price-point, I believe the Fire HD 10 to be the best bang for the buck, without question

title: BUYER BEWARE. Decent stand but the manufacturer is using deceptive practices!
text:
After much debate of which brand of monitor stand I should buy I decided to go with the Fleximounts M06 model despite seeing the Loctek D5D for 13 dollars cheaper on Amazon. The reason being I could only find reviews on the Fleximounts stands and although I was fairly certain the two are the same products under different brand names, the stated specs are not the same for both and I didn't want to get the cheaper brand only to find out it has cheaper craftsmanship. I decided to eat the extra 13 dollars for some peace of mind and made the purchase. A couple days later I RECEIVED A LOCTEK D5D!

This is totally unacceptable. Not only is the practice of selling the same product under different brand and model names to create the illusion of market competition fraudulent but I didn't even receive the item I ordered which is false advertising, completely deceptive and done in bad faith. There was no mistake, my invoice shows what I ordered and yet I didn't even get what I paid for. At this point, trying to straighten out the situation for 13 dollars is more trouble than it's worth since in the end I need a dual monitor stand.

As for the product itself, so far it does what it's supposed to. Build quality seems decent although it does have slight wobble/sag from the stresses of it's own weight so the monitors have the tendency to not sit perfectly straight, and when placed next to each other it can highlight the asymmetry. This hasn't mattered too much in my usage scenario, however, since I am constantly moving monitor positions which is what I bought it for to begin with. Compared to the much more expensive Amazon Basics articulating arm stand this could be a good second choice given it can do most of the same positioning albeit not quite the same flexibility and range of motion but that comes at a price point over a hundred dollars lower so it seems like a decent trade off.

Currently it's holding a Acer GN276HL and a AOC i2769Vm and so far (one week) had no issues. Both are 27" LED screens. It supports their weight fine and unlike what some reviews have stated I can place them side to side in landscape although in that position the mounts can't extend toward you their full length given the fact that the base arm is a solid piece of metal that only pivots at the bottom instead of having a joint that actually extends toward the front. The farthest forward it seems the monitors can get positioned like that is about the halfway mark.

In the end I'm happy with what the stand can do but the business practices of this company are unforgivable and potential buyers should be aware of them. The two models are exactly the same, be sure to check which one is selling for less and get that one. It's amazing that Amazon allows these practices to continue especially from a direct competitor and shows the slacking off in quality control and consumer protections from their company in recent years. It's the reason I still don't pay for their Prime services.

2. It had to have something better than basic Dolby/DTS processing
3. It had to fit the space requirements

Initially, I was going to just get a sound bar without surround, but I grew to like the sound from my LG OLED. It wasn't bad. However, my C6P has fantastic 3D, while my home theater tv has crosstalk issues that make it unwatchable to me. This left me having to choose between watching a movie in 3D or watching it with 7.1 surround. So I decided to look for a sound bar with 5.1 to 7.1. Unfortunately, there's not a lot of options in that group that have 4K, HDR, Atmos or DTSX.. Well, there are if you want simulated surround.

Originally, I had listed the Nakamichi Shockwafe 7.1 as one of two sound bars I was interested in. So when I started looking again, the Ultra 9.2 was listed... Certainly there was a catch! No, there's no catch. 1000W system, 4K HDR passthrough, Dolby processing and DTS:X. Checked the measurements to be sure I could fit this all in the bedroom... Requirements met!

While in transit, I noticed the lack of Atmos/TrueHD and the lack of Dolby Vision. An oversight on my part. Perhaps I'm used to home theater receivers... When I recently bought an Onkyo RZ920, the flagship model, there was no question about HDR, Dolby Vision, Atmos or DTS:X. A flagship audio component should be be just that... The model that does it all, no questions asked. So, when purchasing the Nakamichi Shockwafe Ultra 9.2, I assumed no questions asked. After all, this is Nakamichi, a brand that years back was considered one of the great audiophile brands. Still, having read posts on AVSForum, it appears these things (7.1 TrueHD decoding and Dolby Vision passthrough) can be added via firmware updates, should Nakamichi decide to do so. Not likely though seems to be the general feeling as sound bars take sides in the Dolby vs DTS war.

One other thing of note is that this system is intended to have the subwoofers at the rear since the rear speakers also plug into them with RCA plugs. You can place them at the front and run the included cables, but they're about 16ft long. The cables are also about the same thickness of the cable to your phone's wired earbuds. I replaced mine with heavier 25ft RCA cables.

No regrets though. Despite the lack of native 7.1 TrueHD or Dolby Vision, I would still be searching for something if I wanted everything. That's just the way sound bars are.

Setup was simple enough. Unpack, plug in the HDMI cables and power cords. Connect the rear speakers to the subwoofers (be sure to connect left rears to the left subwoofer and right rears to the right subwoofer) and turn it all on. The subwoofers automatically pair (via bluetooth) to the sound bar.

First impressions were not what I expected. I played Guardians of the Galaxy 2 via the LG Netflix app. It seemed muddled. Turns out there were a few things going on, but after tweaking the settings and sitting a little further back, everything was good!

My primary movie settings are...
DSP: Off (Movie setting adds more bass, but the clarity of the sound gets taken out back)
Pure: Off (enables DTS Neural:X processing/upmixing)
Bass: 7 (after a lot of testing with Passengers, 6 or 7 seems to be about the highest setting before voices were affected)
Treble: 7 (just to match the Bass setting)
Center: 10 (helps with the voice clarity)
SR: 7 (I noticed almost no change between 1 to 10 while watching movies, but while listening to music, it was night and day)
SB: 7 (I noticed almost no change between 1 to 10 while watching movies, but while listening to music, it was night and day)

Now, you might be wondering, what do I compare this to.
Well, that's not easy or fair to answer... My home theater system is an LG 86UH9500 tv, Onkyo RZ920 receiver, Oppo UDP 203 4k player, with Klipsch Forte speakers (front), Klipsch KSC-C1 (center), Klipsch WB14 speakers (surround), Acoustic Research M1 speakers (rear), and a Velodyne subwoofer. This is like comparing a soccer mom's mini van to a Porsche 911, and thus not a fair comparison. What would be fair though is perhaps to compare to the Logitech Z906 system I have connected to the computer.

The Logitech Z906 is a true 5.1 surround system that at full price will cost you $400. Now, the Z906 has flaws. It hasn't been updated in years, and it doesn't have HDMI inputs, so it's not a good option for a home theater setup unless you don't mind using optical/coax and being limited to basic Dolby and DTS processing. Despite all that, used it for years to watch movies on the computer in the bedroom. That being said, if Logitech had ever updated it with HDMI and 4K HDR passthrough, I would have bought that without a second thought since I'm familiar with it.

Coming back to the Ultra 9.2, the sound quality is good. I'm not going to spend hours comparing apples and oranges, but with years of the Z906, I'd say the sound quality of the speakers here are just as good, but technologically, there's more of them, and they do a lot more with DTS:X and Neural:X supporting it. I've spent a bit of time with it watching the first 2 Hunger Games movies in 4K (as well as testing a bunch of movies while setting up the audio) and I've been pleased with the results.

The only real weakness I find is the subwoofers. There's 2 of them, and I expected a lot more room shaking punch. They're really about the same as the subwoofer that comes with the Z906, except they're downward firing while the Logitech is front firing. The impact is right about the same when I gave it the Jurassic Park test. T-Rex won't scare anyone or anything with either. Safe to say, the home theater Velodyne makes things fall down, but again, that's not a fair comparison. Also the placement could be a factor. Firmware updates since the original release also make them a bit heavier sounding.

I have experienced some odd issues since setting up the Nakamichi. The UHD player sometimes appears to have a stroke and believes it no longer has an HDCP 2.2 connection and reverts to 1080p. Twice now has my TV had a stroke and just starts turning 3D on and off for no reason. And a few times now my Roku 4 picture looks like it was put through a blender and reprocessed in 8bit pixelated gaming Minecraft blocks, and the issue appears to be with HDCP 2.2 going AWOL. The last issue is related to startup. I use a Logitech Harmony remote, and when turning everything on, the Nakamichi input will change as intended, but then it will for no reason decide it wants to be on ARC (HDMI 1) and switch back. This is an issue after starting up, and it doesn't always happen. It seems I need to wait at least 15 seconds before changing the input, otherwise it will always go right back to ARC or won't change at all. I'm hoping this gets worked out with firmware.

Lastly, I mentioned a lack of Dolby Vision and 7.1 TrueHD. Dolby Vision isn't on a lot of components. If you happen to have an LG TV and an Oppo player, you can simply use the HDMI audio out of the player to plug into the player, and leave the HDMI video to the TV. In the case of 7.1 TrueHD, you can set your UHD player to PCM instead of bitstream to maintain lossless audio, as suggested on AVSForum. However, you'll want to change it back for DTS:X audio. Personally, I say just leave it on bitstream, and disable Pure mode so that Neural:X can just do its thing. Yes, it's lossy audio then, but I'd be amazed if anyone could tell the difference on a sound bar system. Just the same way 192 bitrate MP3s work fine on your phone with earbuds, but you'll notice it if you play that same MP3 on a high end audio system.

So let's end this. The Nakamichi Ultra 9.2 is a one of a kind. It's a real 7.2/9.2 surround system with DTS:X, and 4K HDR passthrough. In the sound bar market, there's nothing else like it. It achieves what it set out to do, and Nakamichi should be proud of it. Yes, there's room for improvement, and I'm sure Nakamichi knows this, but only time will tell what comes next.

I would probably give this 4 out of 5 because of the lack of lossless TrueHD and Dolby Vision since this is the flagship, and it is Nakamichi. However, I'm going to let it slide because you can work arounds stated above. There's the issues I've run into as well, but I'm confident firmware updates will resolve it. A few interactions with support have left me feeling Nakamichi really wants to be liked the same way they were long ago. It's under warranty, so I have time if firmware fixes are not an option. For what this is, a 7.2/9.2 sound bar surround system, there's currently no equal.

UPDATE: November 12, 2018
Nakamichi has announced an update that will now include Dolby Atmos and Dolby Vision. This update will be available for those of us who already own the system via firmware. This is a big deal! Nakamichi already had a superior soundbar system here, but now it's going to even better.

I've lived with this system for nearly a year now, and the Shockwafe 9.2 has remained everything I hoped for as a bedroom system. I stand firm in that if you can afford a real surround system that includes an A/V receiver, and stand alone speakers, and the technical knowledge to set it up, that THAT is a far superior experience. However, for ease of use, space saving, and lower cost, THIS will obliterate whatever speakers your TV has, and give you a home theater experience from a soundbar system that no other can provide.

UPDATE: February 2, 2019
Nakamichi for the last month has been providing owners of the 9.2 with the firmware upgrade. After the announcement, I purchased a Panasonic DP-UB820 4K player since Oppo went out of business, and I wanted a good player with Dolby Vision.

With the Nakamichi 3.0/3.1 firmware, it does indeed let you use Dolby Atmos and Dolby Vision now, however there's problems, and it's a problem with ARC, Roku, and 4K discs.

With the new Dolby enabled firmware, there's a 5~7 second audio delay. I've also had issues with audio suddenly sounding like it's coming out of a tin can. Nakamichi has stated there could be random audio drop outs as well, and users on AVS Forum have complained about it.

That said, I downgraded back to the 1.0c firmware, the last update before the Dolby upgrade. If Nakamichi fixes the issues, I'll return to it. With or without the Dolby Atmos/Vision update, I still say the best soundbar you can get, and the best you can do without getting a real home theater system.

title: Would Recommend
text:
I purchased this product for the first time roughly six months ago with previous experience with other HDMI cables. In recent past, I purchased the most expensive cables offered in hopes that the price meant the quality would be better and it would last me a life time. This was a mistake, because those cables only lasted a few months at best. I purchased this cable as a last resort with not much hope for the quality. However, I made a false judgement, as the quality is impeccable and better than the other unnecessarily expensive cables I had bought. Do not waste your time with any other cable thinking that the price means it will last; with this cable you get excellent quality for a below average price.
The package arrived exactly on the expected arrival date. I purchased it with the intent of streaming movies onto my TV from my Lenovo Yoga laptop since I don’t have a smart tv. Being able to stream anything from my computer onto my tv cancels out the need to have a smart tv for just about anyone. A $12 investment into a cable is better than a $700 smart TV. I have purchased the 15-foot cable both times. Its over double the length, for only a couple dollars more so it’s more bang for your buck. The long length allows me to walk around with my laptop, not worry about tripping over a stretched cable, and I can sit far away from the tv with my laptop in my lap. The only complaint I have is that the cable tends to fall out of my laptop occasionally if I move around too much. This however could simply be my own fault, and nothing of the manufacturers fault.
I was worried that because the price of the product is very low, the streaming quality would be poor. I decided to take the chance and buy it anyway, and I was thoroughly surprised and impressed. The quality of the image is crisp and clear. The physical quality of the cable is strong and seems built to last for years. I had to repurchase this HDMI cable recently not because the first one failed me, but only because I left it at a friend’s house and somehow it got lost. I was distraught, as I remembered how long it took me to find a quality cable the first time. However, I was able to look through my amazon past orders and found the exact same cable and repurchased it with only one click. The second one I bought I am satisfied with as well. It arrived on time, the quality if it was just as good, and it is just as sturdy as the last one. I have purchased this item twice and both times had very good experiences with the seller and the product. I am extremely satisfied with this customer service and product and would recommend it to anyone looking into purchasing a micro HDMI to HDMI cable.
You can pay anywhere from $5 to $30 for a micro HDMI to HDMI cable, but why would you? This cable is sturdy, reliable, and is excellent quality. The seller provided great customer service which I was relieved about because I’ve had terrible experiences with amazon purchases in the past. The company also shipped it quickly, as soon as my card was processed, I got an email saying it was shipped. The market for HDMI cables is very wide and lots of competition and choice are available, they ignored the prices that their competition set and lowered it quite a bit to win over the customers and my business. Don’t waste your time looking past this HDMI cable, it won’t let you down.

title: High-end anti fatigue mat that is reasonably priced & Made in USA
text:
After going through a couple of cheaper foam mats earlier and now having used this ComfortElite anti fatigue mat made of single core polyurethane, I can tell you that not all anti fatigue mats are made same or feel same. This mat feels like heaven under my feet and it significantly eased fatigue in legs, knees, lower back and provided a more comfortable standing experience. I now enjoy standing for longer while working and been able to get the most benefit out of my standing desk.

After so so results with ordinary foam mats I did some research and realized I need a special mat specifically made for long-time standing. I was determined to find a good anti fatigue mat that also doesn’t break the bank. After lots of research almost to obsessive levels, my parameters for choosing my ideal anti-fatigue mat were clear. The mat has to be made of high density single core polyurethane as every expert’s recommendation seems to point to polyurethane being the best material for a durable, flexible mat that does not lose it’s buoyancy over time. The mat also needs to have non-trip bevelled edges, no skid bottom and non-slip surface. Other factors were size, thickness and aesthetics. After running through my criteria and reviewing some options, I decided to take chance on this ComfortElite mat as it has all the features of my ideal anti-fatigue mat, priced relatively lower compared to other mats with similar features and most importantly it is Made in USA. I also liked the transparency in the product description for this mat regarding the material, construction and the country of make which I could not find with some of the other mats.

I am happy to say this mat hasn’t disappointed me and it definitely lived up to it's ‘anti fatigue’ purpose. In fact I liked it so much that I bought a second mat for my kitchen. At a generous size of 2ft by 3ft (note that this measurement is including the the bevelled edges which take almost 1 inch on each side) this mat perfectly fits my stand up desk as well as in front of my kitchen range. With the 3/4 inch thickness there is substantial cushion under the foot, but is also dense enough that you don’t feel like you are sinking to the floor. There is no strong odor or toxic smell out of the box with this mat. The diamond patterned polyester knit top makes it anti-slip and also aesthetically appealing that it can be used in a home or in an office set-up. All in all this mat is well worth the investment that I have recommended these to several of my colleagues & friends!

title: an SD Card is THE critical component for this scanner (it won't work without one).
text:
The features purported by Uniden for the BCD436HP are awesome- as long as the unit works. This scanner is not Plug & Play and it relies on the SD card for critical functions and storage. If your card reader slot is defective, it won't read the SD card and your scanner won't get past the initial power-up sequence. (it’s the equivalent of trying to use your computer without a hard drive). If your SD card becomes damaged, corrupt or otherwise non-functioning- the scanner will not work until you reformat and reinstall the database to the card. [The common error with the BCD436HP seems to be the following: SD Card File Error, Use Sentinel 'Clear User data operation to initialize SD card].

The Uniden support site and related downloads are antiquated and not intuitive. I found better help from the various discussion groups & blogs on the issue. After exhausting all troubleshooting avenues, I returned the item.

Troubleshooting the above issues appears to have limited success to the users that encounter this problem. This scanner should have a by-pass mode that allows use of the scanner without the SD card. It doesn’t.

In my opinion, the BCD436HP would be a cool backup to a more reliable, self-contained unit like the BCD325P2.

If you do buy the BCD436HP, make copies of your SD card (as formatted by the Sentinel software). This should allow the user to simply replace a corrupt or non-functioning card with a copy and get you back into operation with minimal frustration.

title: Works as advertised but charger tip is a little short for HP Elitebook x360 G2
text:
TLDR: charger tip for N36 was too short for my laptop, kept unplugging; cut with a knife to expose more metal part and works (stays in) much better

I travel for work quite a bit so I wanted to get an extra charger for my work laptop (HP Elitebook x360 G2). I settled for this product as the reviews were pretty solid, price point seemed reasonable and the charger also includes two USB ports which I thought would be convenient to charge my phone.

Product works as advertised and comes with a mini-guide to let you know which chargers you should use. The charger tips are pretty easy to switch in/out as well. For my laptop I used the N36 charger tip and when plugged in, the thing charges my laptop without issue (i.e., computer recognizes the charger, doesn't pop up with the "unrecognized charging device" window). USB ports also work nicely.

The charger does get quite hot when in use for a while, but I think that's pretty typical for chargers in my experience. The main reason I am docking stars from my review is because the charger tip is slightly shorter than my original manufacturers charger. You can see in the image I took that one of the tips is like a millimeter or two longer than the other. In this instance, size DOES matter.

One little wiggle or movement and the thing comes slightly unplugged from my laptop and stops charging. Due to the size issue the charger tip is incredibly sensitive and can even unplug by itself if the laptop is simply leaning in that direction (i.e., from gravity). If you mostly use your laptop at your desk it will be less of an issue, but it's still likely to come unplugged every once in a while.

To address the shortness/length issue I used an X-ACTO knife to carefully carve away a millimeter or so of the black plastic casing around the metal tip. So far this seems to be working and the plug stays in much better.

title: Excellent Calibration results for my new 4k tv
text:
Purchased to calibrate a new Samsung 4k TV. The bottom-line is that this device produced amazing results on my TV and for that I give it 5 stars with some caveats. The process was really slow to get my fire stick and so I sat with the actual Calman device for 3 weeks and could not use it (I almost returned it but glad I did not). The software was a little tricky to get set up and the instructions could be improved but the technical help was outstanding. Kudos to JP in the tech dept for instantly responding to my questions on the installation and connections.
Once it was all installed and working, moving through the menus was really easy. If you have an older plasma this is still a great device but on my Panasonic I was not able to adjust Gamma and white balance (which are critical in my opinion). My new TV had all of these advanced picture options. As an additional bonus I have a free fire stick to use. Again the real results are what matters for me and the new 4k TV now looks amazing post calibration!!!
***Update*** After calibrating 3 of my TVs (Plasma, 2 LEDs including a 4k) this device makes a world of difference. The before and after adjustments really show the dramatic difference. Now that I know how to adjust I can complete a full calibration in 20 minutes or less.
On top you get a free fire stick so for the price this is so much better than getting a slightly cheaper calibration dvd.

title: More than a pretty face
text:
I've owned the Venere 2.5's for 6 months now and have greatly enjoyed them. These towers can dig surprisingly low, a professional reviewer noted they had usable output down to 28hz. Watching the movie Oblivion with them running full range through an 90wpc Denon with no sub woofer I was completely blown away. The bass hit hard enough to feel it in my chest 12 feet away and I didn't miss my sub woofer at all. I've since added dual 12" subs to free up some headroom on the receiver and increase clarity at louder SPL levels and it's even better. The tweeter is magical for the female voice, It just sounds right to my ear and is very smooth and non-fatiguing, I find myself listening to music longer than I have with any other pair of speakers. During a movie or show when they have a Jazz band or musical performance they are stunning and chill inducing. That said one of the reason why those musical interludes stand out so much is that these speakers are very revealing, so much so that poorly recorded or produced music/tv is noticeable. Feed them high quality sources and you're in for a real treat.

The Venere lineup in my opinion is a warm speaker (bass boost between 80-150hz) with a very smooth neutral top end that rolls off before getting harsh. They were crafted after the companies flagship speaker the Aida ($120k) with the same general cabinet shape and knowledge they gained from that project. Of course they're not in the same league in sound nor craftsmanship, but they were able to use lessons learned from that project to make these. In my view these do well as a hybrid music/home theater system. They're excellent at music, but for strictly home theater (no music) purposes you'd be better off with some higher efficiency speakers with horn loaded tweeters for better dynamics IMO. They still perform admirably in home theater duty and have more than enough output to fill a good sized living area.

They're easily the nicest looking speakers I've seen under $5k, my wife likens them to a pair of Italian stilettos. You're definitely paying more for the superior craftsmanship and good looks, but these are quite large speakers and if you don't have a dedicated Home theater room style matters. There's not a parallel surface on these, the base gently tilts backward to time align the drivers and they have a Lyre shaped cabinet with an automotive grade paint finish that is highly reflective. The tapered design is especially nice because when you toe them in to get the right stereo image they don't look awkwardly placed like many rectangular speakers do. You can satisfy the wife approval factor with tiny form speakers that are lackluster in sound or get a sculpted piece of art like these that's capable of rocking the house. Of note, these are the first speakers made in China by Sonus Faber to drive down costs (Their handmade Italian models run between $6-$120k). They were crafted under the supervision of the main factory and the employees were trained in Italy. The fit and finish of the speakers is excellent and is in no way compromised, of course the Italian hardwood leather-clad higher end models are even more stunning. The vast majority of the high end speaker companies including B&W take a similar approach to deliver high quality sound for a lower entry price.

Are they the greatest speakers in the world? No, but they have an excellent balance of musicality, good looks, and are just plain nice to listen to. If aesthetics don't matter you can likely do better for less money, but sound is very subjective and highly dependent on the room you place it in. What sounds great in one room may sound terrible in another, before making a purchase of this level you owe it to yourself to audition a few different pairs in your own home before making a decision.

title: Let me be clear, you cannot go wrong with the MacBook.
text:
Just so we're clear, I purchased mine at the local BB store during a one-day fantastic promo sale for 1/3 off the weekend before Christmas, after months of daily online checking everywhere for the best pricing. That said, where I purchased the machine, doesn't detract from my review. Let me be clear, you cannot go wrong with the MacBook.

Initially I was undecided between the MacBook and the MacBook Air (13"). The main factors between the machines for me was pricing, USB slots, memory, and the quality of the camera. The MBA has less memory in their base model, has on board USB slots and a decent on-board camera. Out of the box it was approx $999. The MB has no USB slots, a lesser quality camera, but more RAM and more on board storage, plus it has the butterfly keyboard and a retina screen. The one-day deal at Best Buy I found put the MB at $999, so the pricing was comparable.

For what I use the system for (e.g., internet browsing, word processing, spreadsheet preparation, FaceTime, movie watching) I did not need a system that was overly "souped up". The MB suited my needs. The butterfly keyboard is noticeably more comfortable on my fingertips and hands than a regular keyboard. The on board mouse pad is very easy to use, especially with El Capitan.

I was able to get over the lack of USB by purchasing the $19 USB-C to USB dongle. Its really not that big of a deal. The MB is smaller than a regular piece of paper and very light. Its an excellent purchase. I have no regrets, except getting it sooner. I have used it every day. The battery life on it is amazing. The battery lasts for about 9 hours in use and much longer on standby.

Set up was flawless. Out of the box to using it was 20 minutes. title: Very capable chromebook, fanless operation is great, some small nit picks.
text:
This chromebook is very capable with a powerful i5 processor and an adequate amount of memory to keep dozens of tabs operating at full speed. I wish there were a version of the i5 based Pixelbook with 16GB memory. The i7 based pixelbook with 16GB memory is almost twice the price; memory is what chromebooks love the most, few will need the power of the i7 processor. With 12 tabs open I am consuming 6GB of the 8GB available, so there is some wiggle room but not a lot. WIsh the memory was easily upgradeable.

The power switch is near the front of the laptop on the side and I find myself pressing it accidentally as I reposition the laptop on my lap. A more conventional power button on the keyboard would make more sense. Thankfully chrome OS prompts me for what I want to do when its pressed.

The screen is crisp and clear, but having become accustomed to monitors and laptops with 16:9 form factor its weird going back to a screen that's 4:3. Youtube is more cramped in 4:3 format.

USB-C is in theory amazing, a single connector that can be used for power, video, audio, everything. However the realities of USB-C are that many devices are incompatible with each other. I have an HP USB-C docking station that is very good. The Pixelbook doesn't even recognize the device or accept a charge from the docking station. I would prefer one HDMI port to be present to eliminate the need for a dongle for presentations.

The aluminum case is very sleek looking, but I do find it a little slick when carrying the laptop. I can see myself dropping this if I don't take care.

The touchpad is totally amazing. Until you experience a touchpad this good, you don't know what you've been missing. The pixelbook is totally silent thanks to it having no fan.

Shortly after setup I experienced very poor battery life, less than 2 hours and the laptop got quite hot. An Android service was using all available CPU cycles constantly. I did a powerwash, even though I had the pixelbook just 24 hours, the laptop works great now. Not sure what went wrong during initial setup. The beauty of the Chrome OS platform is that rests and power washes are a small inconvenience, setup is pretty much seamless.

Te keyboard is a little cramped compared to larger laptops, I find myself pressing the wrong key more often than I'd like. The operation of the keyboard however is awesome. The Google assistant feature is more useful than I thought it would be. It may become one of my favorite features.

The ability to run Android apps coupled with android messages all on the Pixelbook means I can do pretty much all things I need to from this device. I can relegate my Pixel phone to only times I'm away from home. This device can do pretty much anything you need, and does so quickly and without fuss.

With some chromebooks I've run low on storage, many come with just 16GB. This chromebook comes with 128GB, a huge amount of storage for Chrome OS. I won't have to send time managing disk space with this unit.

title: The verdict is still out
text:
First off the my purchase was an Amazon Warehouse Deal meaning it was pre-owned, The product arrived with all accessories and appeared like new. It comes with everything you need to hook it up plus it has nice voltage displays for input and output. The fans cycle on for very short cycles, I understand that it saves power but, I found it kinda annoying. Over the the span of 3.5 days the voltage never varied staying at 124 volts output. Initial connection was made with the batteries at 27.4 volts and instantly an arc and one fuse blew. I replaced it and reconnected power. Depending on the time of day input voltage stayed between 24.8 and 27.4 the unit was able to load 500 watts with no problem so, I was satisfied and ignored the initial problem. I put it into service running a continuous load of about 200 watts - 2 ceiling fans in an off grid horse barn. Day one and two no problems, about 194 amp-hours were used and was as expected. Day three, when I got home I checked everything and no problems were found except I had doubled my AH usage vs the first two days and my battery voltage was 26.2. I verified my loads and all my wiring I couldn't find any problems and not having enough time I took it offline for safety concerns. Day four, batteries were on float at 27.4 volts 51AH were used in the previous 24 hours (normal). I put a 400 watt load on the inverter and the red fault light was flashing and no output voltage. I powered it down, disconnected everything and restarted it, everything seemed normal until both fuses blew after about 2 hours. I removed the inverter and to the bench we went, I installed two fuses and applied 25.3 volts - 24 volt power system at 100% charge and the fuses blew immediately, I replaced them a 3rd time and instantly the same problem. I don't know what cause the sudden increase in draw nor the fuses to blow instantly. Hopefully the manufacturer will get the inverter back and let us all know. I've arranged the return to Amazon and thought I'd order another one because the price isn't bad, well due to errors in the description I accidentally ordered a 12 volt instead of the 24 volt. I have another barn that runs on 12 volts but, I'm going to put trust in the powers that be and return this one without even putting power to it. Barns are not cheap and the animals inside are priceless so, I'm marking this one up as fate not wanting me to use this inverter. I may purchase another one in the future because part of me believes the problem with the inverter was caused by its first owner. However there is another couple options in the same price rage and I will try one of them to try and find the most reliable and efficient one.

Notes: the solar system and batteries had been running DC lighting and a modified sine wave inverter before this upgrade. All AC lights and fans were installed to code and tested using an inverter generator and were run for minimum of 700 hours or one month on generator or modified sine wave inverter power. The 24 volt DC bulbs and 24 to 12 volt DC to DC adapter never had a problem even when the inverter did.

title: Very Nice Alternate Solution To Built-in Television Speakers
text:
I bought the Polk 2000 IHT Soundbar with the hope that it would provide better sound than my TV speakers. Mission accomplished. The soundbar provides a very nice surround effect and the sound quality is what I expect from Polk. I also have a five speaker (Polk RTA-11TL tower speakers, Polk M3 II rear speakers, and Polk CS200 center speaker) surround system. The soundbar does not provide the full surround sound that a front and rear system provides. However, the surround effect is very nice. You can hear the main sound that sounds like it is coming from the television as well as background sounds that seem to come from the extreme left or right. For the most part, the sound is clear and rich. Very low bass sound causes the soundbar to rattle, which I find to be annoying. I used the bass adjustment on the remote to turn the bass level all the way down, which was a big help without losing the richness. I am guessing that if I had spent more money to buy a soundbar with a separate sub-woofer this would not be an issue. I had a little trouble programming my TV remote to control the soundbar, but I was able to do it successfully nonetheless. One thing I do not like is that the indicator lights are on the top of the unit rather than on the front so you can see what you are doing when adjusting the volume or selecting a source. It would also be nice if there was an actual indicator showing the increase or decrease of the volume or bass level when you adjust them. I saw a one star review that complained that the surroundbar does not come with a power supply. I thought that was true with mine as well. Then I realized that the power supply was packaged at the end of the box that was damaged in shipping and got lost in transit. I called Polk support and had a power supply within a week.

Overall, for the price (I paid roughly $100.00), this is a nice surround sound system and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a low price solution to improve the sound quality from your television.

title: Pretty good cooler that is misunderstood.
text:
I think this cooler is misunderstood.

One review mentioned that the contact surface on this cooler is round, and the CPU package is rectangular. But this is not a problem because your actual CP chip is about 16mm square, and the cooler surface is about 28mm round. So it more than covers the area where the heat is generated.

Second, I don't think people are evaluating the cooling capacity correctly. The fan on this cooler has a maximum RPM of about 3000 RPM. My Coolermaster 612 EVO has a max fan speed of 1300RPM. To use this cooler, you have to set the fan curve to match the fan. If you don't, it will perform very poorly.

On my system with a i7-6850k, and with all six cores at 100%, my hottest core runs about 55C.

The mating surface is extremely flat and smooth. This is because it is a turned part, which makes it easy to machine to very tight tolerances. Compare this to other coolers that have mating surfaces that are "flattened" on a belt sander. This may be cheap, but it's just not possible to get a very flat surface this way.

The mating force is well controlled with four individual springs. My 612 EVO had a single lever that applied too much force to the CPU.

The one downside is that because the fan runs at higher RPM, it is louder than some others.

title: Semi-Modularity likely brings down the price point, and clutter factor is relatively low
text:
This PSU is a relatively cheap-for-its-class PSU offered by EVGA, possessed of some great rail distribution for an "only" 750W supply. Its Bronze certification means it may not be the most efficient PSU available, but it makes up for it by providing good, clean, constant power.

Being a semi-modular design, it 'cuts corners' somewhat compared to full modularity, but the good thing is that the only 'fixed' cables are the ones you'd be using 9 times out of 10 anyways -- 24-pin for the mobo, 4+4 (8)-pin for the CPU, and two 6+2-pin PCI-e lines for an extension card of some sort (likely a GPU). These are routed out of the left side of the PSU when mounted fan-down, making this a good choice for a bottom-mounted PSU (as you can direct the cables into the back panel for good cable management purposes)... but not so much for top-mounted models.

The modular connectors support a variety of (packed-in) power connectors, including 2 daisy-chained Molex strings for powering 'dumb' fans or LEDs, another pair of 6+2 PCI-e cables (for powering a second high-draw GPU, or two other standard PCI devices), and 3 triple-connector SATA chains for powering ODDs/HDDs/SSDs, etc. (and clearly intended to sit behind the 5.25" rack, 3.5" rack, and 2.5" rack, respectively, or any mixture of the three, and power up to 9 devices). A second CPU output is also present for servers or the rare multi-CPU build.

Aesthetically, it's not glitzed-up with LEDs or anything, but neither is it unnecessarily drab. The PSU, as seen in a bottom-mounted configuration, is just a featureless black box, albeit with EVGA branding stickers cleverly disguised as useless nonsense (kidding!) such as safety precautions and electrical values. I mean, if you really want to brag about having a Bronze-cert, semi-modular, cost-effectiveness-oriented PSU in your 1337 g4m3r rig, go for it. In the end, it's just a functional PSU, albeit one with a bit more tolerance than the truly bargain-basement models.

title: It sounds average at best as far as audio quality
text:
I first spotted this at the 2018 CES in Vegas and it blew me away. The speaker is very buoyant, and floats with the water line below the woofers. Basically, you just toss it in the water and listen to it. That's how Altec Lansing had it demo'd as well, in a water tank. I tested it by submerging it fully, while it was playing, and pressing a few buttons. No issue.

Now that i have one, I have taken a closer look at it. It sounds average at best as far as audio quality. Good enough for some fun on the water, but really not as good as I believe it should be. I subtracted one star for that. It is loud though, so you can really crank it up. It has a strobe light you can turn on and off, which really seems kind of silly. I can't see ever needing or wanting it on. It also has lights that light up the woofers and can pulse to the beat of the music. You can also toggle between 12 different colors of the light effect. Kind of cool, I guess.

The power input has a plastic cap on it with an O-ring. You press it closed and turn it to click it closed. That is the waterproofing for power. Seems good enough, but they never show it in pictures. The bluetooth pairing is very simple. It has NFC so you can just tap your phone to the sweet spot and it pairs instantly (if you have NFC on your phone). One cool feature is you can link 2 of these speakers together for stereo sound. It links wirelessly. That's awfully expensive at 399 each and I really can't see a need for it. One of these is loud enough. If the sound quality was better maybe it would be more useful.

Overall, the speaker system is loud enough, big enough, and "cool looking" enough. I haven't had time to test battery life or start tossing it in the lake. Looking to have some fun this summer out on the lake....

UPDATE JULY 2018

I have since used this on a number of occasions. I have yet to run the battery out on any boat trips. I am again not really impressed with the sound quality. It is kind of tinny...like an AM radio station. Not much bass or mid. Also, I experienced what another guy dud and my subs just "shut off" after long use on a hat 95 degree day. It still played, but way quieter with horrible sound quality.

title: Perfect Gaming Laptop at a Great Price
text:
I've had this laptop for about a week which has given me enough time to really run it hard and see what it can do. I'll go ahead and do a pros/cons list to make it a little easier.

Pros:
-Boots INSANELY fast with the SSD, which I would wholeheartedly recommend.
-Graphics for gaming in general are absolutely stunning. No problems running at max settings with a gorgeous FPS for most games.
-The screen is matte and I don't have the glare problem I had with other glossy screens.
-Color on the screen is gorgeous and bright.
-The color steelseries Keyboard is AWESOME and can be customized to specific color schemes.
-The keyboard is lovely, even with the windows key on the right side. It took some getting used to, but its just second nature now. And the keys are perfect and aren't noisy at all when typed on.
-The speakers on the front of the laptop are actually quite robust and it could certainly be used in a pinch if you don't have external speakers or headphones. They don't sound tinny and there's even a good amount of bass.
-The mousepad is one of the better mousepads I've seen on a laptop. I haven't figured out if there's a way to disable it, since I use a USB mouse, but it's in the perfect position to not get touched when playing games. I think I've only accidentally hit it once when playing and it didn't screw me up, really.
-The fan turbo button is a fantastic way to amp up the cooling while playing more graphics-intensive games. The WADS area of the keyboard can get warm, but not uncomfortably so when the fans have been turned on.
-The brushed metal look on the whole laptop is really nice looking. I even like the dragon MSI symbol on the back of it.
-HDMI out and supports multiple monitors, which is also really nice.

Cons:
-Came with Norton (blech) but it took seconds to uninstall, so no probs there.
-Drivers may need to be updated before you can get the most out of the graphics card, but again this is quite easy to do.
-Windows key is on the right side, but I've already learned it's position with muscle memory and it's been no problem.
-Crappy battery life, but this is more of a desktop replacement, so I'm really not concerned about that. I didn't buy this for anything but gaming, really.

That's really it! I've honestly been running this laptop through it's paces trying to get it to lag and it's been sailing through everything I throw at it so far. If you're on the fence about picking this up, I say go for it! This computer will be home for me for quite a while, I think. Fantastic build and all the bells and whistles of a gaming rig with the portability of a laptop. I'd give it 6 stars if i could!

title: Perfect... Tried the rest, this was the best and lowest priced
text:
I bought 4 "yes 4" different brands (Pleson, Volt shield , Zolid and Casesie) to see which best fit the s6 "We have 3 s6's in the house".

The Zolid barely covers the black border on the s6 but it does manage to cover it, the Volt Shield doesn't even go that wide and is simply too narrow and finally between the Pleson and the casesie brands it's a close comparison.

Out of all of them I can easily say the Pleson in the white packaging is the clearest, and largest of them all. Plus it cost the least!

This Pleson brand is much taller than the others, so you get more protection on the screen towards the front camera and home button.

The only cons I'd give it is:

One out of the 3 pleson brand I ordered came in a brown package instead of the white and it's slightly narrower and not as tall as the version in the white pack. I'm guessing the white pack is the newest version since it says it's a Pleson Plus+. Also instead of a microfiber cloth "which is good to roll up and use to squeegee out the air bubbles" this kit instead comes with a dry and wet scratchy cotton twill pads. But I'm fine with those small gripes as the protectors themselves are extremely clear and offer more protection over the others.

As with any glass protectors if you run into a problem and need to remove it to either re-apply or pick out a piece of lint don't try and hurry and pull it off or you WILL crack them. Just wedge a fingernail under a corner and slowly apply very little pressure until you can hold that corner up about 1/4" off the phone. Now keep holding it at that angle and the glass protectors slowly remove themselves. Now line it up and try again, slowly dropping it onto the screen length wise "bottom to top" while guiding with your thumb and index finger "just don't touch the back!" and there ya go.

title: Paperwhite is great, but get the voyage you won't regret it. A gem for the avid reader
text:
I only write reviews that I feel strongly about, 1 or 5 stars. I love the voyage. I used to have one of the first generation kindles and fell out of love with it and went back to paper books. I got discouraged though, lugging books around and constantly stressing about not having a book for a plane ride or a vacation. The newer kindles looked like big steps up to me! I spent days agonizing over the paperwhite vs the voyage and looked at both in a box store. I also struggled with waiting for the oasis, but I was not interested in the battery in the cover setup or the push buttons that stick out. I finally went with the voyage and could not be happier...but I had to buy two voyages to get there. The first voyage I bought at the box store because I did not want to wait for amazon - I was to excited. Turns out they said it had been sitting around for years and when I got home it was yellow on the top and blue on the bottom -the blue gave me a headache. I returned it and figured I would order from amazon because it would be the latest device of the optimized manufacturing line - it is perfect from amazon, be weary of the box stores. I recommend buying only from amazon because amazon turns over their devices more than the box store and since most of us love amazon, we may as well support them.

I think the voyage is worth the extra money. First, how can you justify that the 2X cost of the paperweight is not worth it if you read thousands of hours - thousands of hours at the movies would cost you many kindles in comparison. Plus I'm a neuroscientist and believe that reading is good for memory and may help reduce cognitive decline in aging , so there what's a $100 in that context! Reading is good for the brain, don't skimp on it the tools that help you read.

The voyage felt better. It is lighter and more comfortable and is way sleeker. The touch buttons are way to cool and though you don't need them, when you are laying just right and don't want to move your hand, they make a huge difference in the experience. I also paid $20 to get rid of the advertising - I have to comment that I think it's pretty sleazy for amazon to hold us hostage with advertising, but I get it, they are running a business and amazon supports my lifestyle so no big deal, but the executive that came up with this idea, well no comment on how I feel about his morals.

Now, one more comment. I have huge hands, I can palm a basket ball. The voyage is not to small for me, but it is hard for me to hold it with one hand with my thumb over the buttons. Not the voyages fault, I just have paddles for hands. I discovered that for one handed holding for big handed people, a case, any case, makes a big difference. With the case I can place the flap between my pointer and middle fingers and hold the voyage quite easily with one hand and it feels more like a book this way too. A good excuse for a case, but if that's not enough of a reason, it auto turns the device on and off, which is great. I know it doesn't sound like much, but not having to press the power button is a nice convenience. Not to mention a case protects the voyage.

So there you have it, if you are deciding between the voyage and paperwhite and have some extra dough, I would say you will be a lot happier with the voyage. That said, you will be super happy with the paperwhite. I have no seen the oasis, so I cannot really make a comparison there.

I also have a subscription to the kindle library, that is a great, I have more than 12 books I want to read on it in the first year, so it should pay for itself. It's free for a month, so check it out.

I would give the voyage 5 thumbs up if I had that many thumbs, so today we can settle for 5 stars!

title: It's not a man-bag, it's a necessity
text:
After plenty of delay, I finally ordered the Full Grain Leather Briefcase from Polare. I wanted something with a bit more character than the other bags I have used for work and carrying work related material. After reading the reviews of both a similarly made briefcase priced approximately 4x as much and one that was almost identical, even in price, I pulled the trigger on the Polare. Why?

When comparing it to the one that was made by that saddle company, I determined that if I use this daily and there are not any problem within 11-12 months, it's a keeper. If there are issues, it has a 1 year guarantee. $200, 2-years under the worst-case-scenario. I also looked at situations where people are now selling one of the saddle company briefcases and they struggle to sell it for half of the amount they have "invested" in the case. The Polare wins the numbers game, prior to purchase. The Polare is advertised as a Full Grain Leather, as is the Saddle company case.

When comparing it to the similarly made and priced briefcases also found online, this case is the only one that is advertised as “100% Pure Full Grain Leather”. Why does this even matter?
Full Grain Leather comes from the top layer of the hide which has ALL of the grain, therefore, FULL grain. This is the highest-quality leather. The second-highest-quality leather is top-grain leather. Top Grain Leather is named top grain because the very top layer is sanded, buffed or shaved off. Top-grain leather is still appropriate for luxury goods. But, know that the durability, and the future patina of the leather, has been compromised by affecting the top most layer of the skin. Top grain leather does not age nicely with use but it is strong and durable. Genuine Leather is the third grade of leather and is produced from the layers of hide that remain after the top is split off for the better grades. The surface can be refinished to resemble a higher grade. It can be smooth or rough. This is also suede. Bonded Leather is the dust and shavings of the leather glued and pressed together. Think fiberboard of the leather world. Leftover scraps are ground together with glue and resurfaced in a process similar to vinyl manufacture. Bonded leather is weak and degrades quickly with use. Genuine and bonded leather can be spray-painted to look like full or top grain leather.

I also preferred the hardware on the Polare over the similarly made and priced cases also found on Amazon. Polare wins the value game, prior to purchase. The Polare is priced within $1 of the other similarly made and priced cases, but made with the highest quality leather.

The Unboxing
With Prime shipping, the case arrived in 2 days, just as advertised. Packaged and wrapped professionally, with an outer weather-proof bag, taped tightly and snuggly. After removing the outer bag, the inner protective covering is more like a breathable sack. Once it is out of the sack, my eyes are in awe of the Brown Leather Suitcase and my nose is filled with the scent of fresh leather.

The Briefcase Material
The briefcase is heavy, of substance, and beautiful. The outer appearance is certainly finished. The leather and the hardware does not exhibit any short-cuts in production or application. The rings and rivets have been placed with precision and done so cleanly. Even the absence of manufacturer's branding is a positive element not to be overlooked. The inner-lining is well-done as well. The top flap of the bag is actually lined with using what appears to be a fully tanned/dyed suede to cover and protect the hardware and sticking used on the top flap. The panels, side-walls and straps are all nicely finished. Using a combination of Leather and Nylon serves the bag well. The rear compartment is fully lined with a nylon material. This inclusion of the nylon lining aids placing laptop and/or my 7-ring planner by allowing both to slide in and out without grabbing or unnecessary rubbing. The front section also benefits from the same nylon lining.

The Briefcase Design
The briefcase has two main compartments, with both being approximately of equal dimensions(3.75 x 15.5 x 11). The front section has 2 inner pockets, each being approximately 5.5 inches wide and 8.5 deep. The pockets(nylon material) are not “cupped” or “squared” at the bottom, but rather flat. My impression is that it will easily handle up to an inch worth or material, or and item that is 8.5 x 5.5 x 1. This really aids in allowing them to collapse when not in use.The second pocket is identical. These pockets on the center divider could easily be used for cables, charging blocks and even small notebooks There are also 2 small pockets on the external side-walls of the briefcase that could be used for things such as a water bottle and/or sunglasses. Finally, there are a large rear pocket, which would easily hold a few legal files or documents, magazines, newspapers, and airline tickets.
There are 8 exterior D-rings can be used to tether external items to the case if you need to use the briefcase as an impromptu backpack. Yes, the shoulder-strap can easily be re-purposed to serve as a backpack-shoulder strap using the D-rings.
The straps allow the case to be closed by 1 strap or 3 straps. The outer straps can be fully removed, leaving on the center strap, or they can be tucked under for optional use. Ultimately, how you use the straps is up to you. The last strap that needs to be mentioned is the internal key strap. This strap is ideal for runaway or spare keys and even the need for an access pass.
This bag is large enough to carry almost everything a person would need for work and can be used as a carry-on during airplane travel as it fits under most airline seats.

Finally, this bag is designed for the “long-game” with no breakable parts such as zippers, buttons or snaps. Durable materials, stitching in lieu of glue, and practical design have been combined to present an excellent case to last for years.

title: This remote is freakin' awesome...and how to create "Skip Forward" button
text:
It's simple for basic users, yet advanced enough that you can program macros, or copy buttons (even from a different remote) or rearrange button functionality. I love how you can lock buttons such as volume or on/off. For example, if you're using a Roku, normally you'd have to hit the "TV" button to switch your device mode then "On/off." With this remote, you can program the power button to shut your TV off no matter which device mode you are in.

I bought this remote specifically for the Roku 3, because I didn't want to use two remotes (one for Roku, one for TV). It's awesome that it's preprogrammed for the Roku, but you can easily program any other device. You can look up any device it supports online and you can also find the owner's manual here: http://shop.inteset.com/ir_remote_control_device_setup_code_search

Also, their support team is great. I emailed them from the website above, and they got back to me really quickly. I didn't know where the "instant replay" (rewind 8 seconds) button was for the Roku. They emailed me and said the instant replay is programmed to the button labeled "last". I preferred to set "instant replay" to the smaller rewind arrow button, so I'll I did was use the "copy" function (see manual) and now both buttons have the "instant replay" capability.

I don't have experience with $200 remote controls, but why would anyone want something that expensive? I feel like this remote can do everything you'll ever need and more!

HOW TO CREATE "SKIP FORWARD BY 10 SECONDS" BUTTON (opposite of instant replay) for Roku or other DVR devices.
1) Press Roku device ("D" Button).
2) Hold setup for a few seconds until it blinks
3) Enter 995 (to program macros)
4) Press “Skip forward” button (I used the small fast forward button). This is the button you’re setting the macro to. The next buttons are the series of commands assigned to your macro.
5) Press the big “fast forward” button.
6) Press “diamond” button once (assuming it’s assigned to nothing. If you skip this step, it fast forwards only a few seconds. Adding a “do nothing” button, is like creating a pause in the macro. The more times you press the diamond button, the longer it will fast forward. I found you only need to press it once to get roughly a 10 second skip forward).
7) Press “Play” button.
8) Press and hold “setup” until it blinks to save your macro.
Now when you press the “Skip forward” button, your show should move ahead 10 seconds, which is a quick way to skip past commercials.

title: Record it, re-play it, enjoy it.
text:
Introduction: I think the first question you probably have is “Why?”, why this camera over say, one of the dozens of 1080p cameras out there and they are getting cheaper by the minute, why this one?... theres one word that answers that: Sensors. Now, you might say that’s not important but think of this: Unless you are a pro at extreme sports, or a no holds-downhiller, you are probably a normal person with a passion for sports and your videos, although entertaining for you...will not make it on the youtube’s most watched, and that’s ok, what sensors bring to the table is the ability to make your videos entertaining. Now, take Skiing for example... how fun is it to watch a video of you going downhill? (from your perspective, mind you), I’ll answer, its not as fun unless its you watching it. Now, add your heart rate thumping like you are about to die, your speed, the elevation going down by the second and a map....and suddenly that video changes to entertaining. This is what this camera gives you! the ability to connect a heart rate monitor to it, and with its integrated GPS, gives you speed, altitude, location..all of that jazz. Your video suddenly is very fun to watch. I have 1 Bandit and two 1080p’s cameras (Yi), yes, the yi records video and its cheaper, but when I go back to the videos...I never watch them, its boring, I find myself going back to videos with this camera and analyzing...”humm, I pressed the brake too much before that turn (when on the bike), or I was flying when I saw that deer too close!”, its just a very big difference. But enough of that, lets talk about the camera itself:

First Use:

This is a gadget, and as such requires you to at least understand it before just jumping in and just making it work. Now, you can do that, just turn it on and record...but where’s the fun in having a gadget but not know how to make it pop? Kidding aside, when you open the box, you get: Batt-Stick (usb stick that contains the battery and the sd card),charging cable, lenses, camera itself (the batt-stick removes from the camera body), mounts (various and it depends on your package).You might want to charge the camera before first use, its just good for these devices, having said that, the folks at Tom Tom know you can’t wait to use it so the camera comes with some charge.
First thing you’ll notice is that the camera itself has a mount that is different from gopro in many ways that are all better: FIrst off, no screws to put the camera on the mount, you press the bottom of the mount and the mount “opens” to be inserted, that’s it, couldn’t be simpler. The second is that the integrated mount rotates on the camera for lack of a better word, it allows you to move the camera position better.
Physical Aspect: The big elephant in the room is that the camera shape is not a go-pro shape. At first that was weird to me, but, it has a reason: The batt-stick, have you ever been on a ski lift, at -10 degrees and try to change the sd card or batter (or both) on a gopro camera? Yep, its not fun at all, on the Yi? its even harder. With this camera, you can do it with gloves! Take out the batt-stick (that contains the sd card) and insert a new one (that you can buy through Tom Tom) and voilá. That alone is enough for me to say that the physical aspect works.

Configuring

I have an android phone (2 years old) and the application for Tom Tom works w/o hiccups (note: you don’t need to have a phone for the camera to work, but its better if you do). You can connect and see what the camera is seeing (which has a big impact on battery because of wifi). The only thing that isnt intuitive on Android is that you physically have to connect to the wifi of the camera (by goings to settings, wifi) before the app can see the camera, I’ve only noticed that it happens when the phone is connected to a previous wifi (like, if Im home), but still, thats a tip/trick that is good to know. Turn on the camera, turn on the wifi on the camera, open the app, then connect to wifi of the bandit directly, then the app works w/o hiccups. What you can do with the app: Start recording, update the camera (firmware), take photos, configure your account, edit/view/share your videos/photos. I wont go into detail about the app because the nature of apps is that they change and I dont want my review to get stale because of that, but, suffice to say, you DONT need a computer to deal with your videos, you might need a lot of storage on your phone...but thats another thing.

Sensors:

Note here, the Bandit has GPS and you can connect a bluetooth heart rate monitor, sorry, no cadence monitor for your bike rides, so I connected a bluetooth Tom Tom heart rate monitor to it and the process was very easy to do (Go to Settings --> General --> Connect --> Sensors --> Heart) after the first connection, if Im wearing it, it connects automatically, same for the remote (Settings --> General -->Connect --> Remote-->press the ON button on the remote for 3 seconds until the LED flashes green three times). Again, after first connection, the remote is recognized.

Remote:

This is arguably one of the best features, the remote that has a light on it! And by light I mean an indicator light, why is that important you ask? Try wearing a camera on your helmet and figuring out if its recording with a remote that has no light indicator. It comes with an arm band that fits over my jackets or I can put it on my handlebars if on the bike. I like the simplicity of it, it just works.

Camera

The most important thing are the images and video, and this camera does not disappoint. I find myself continuously using 1080p 60 frames instead of the higher 4k, yes, 4k looks awesome on a 4k monitor (I tried), but the files are big and truth be told, I never watch my videos full screen so the added resolution for me is not needed. At 1080p 60 frames, I can go downhill hitting 40mph, no issues. In fact, I never change the resolution anymore, it stays put at 1080, 60. Take in consideration something, a file with GPS/Heart Rate at 1080 60, is > 1GB for 6 minutes of recording, so files are big. The camera does not split the GPS/HR info onto another file, its all self-contained.
I took some photos with it (to try them out), and they are not better than my phone (a Motorola), however, its good to know I can just whip this out and take a photo if the need arises.

Mounts

My version came with different mounts for helmets, a gopro conversion one and a bike one, I’ve put them all through the wringer and suffice to say, they work, nothing has broken (and I did a nasty downhill run with the handlebar mount). They are the highest quality mounts I’ve ever tried, these things are solid! (when compared to a couple of gopro mounts I have). My only tip/trick here is that the handlebar mount one is a tripod head, so make sure you tight it really good before heading out or the rocks that you go over will eventually make the camera move.

Using the remote

To use it, press the START button (“red star button”) for 3 seconds until the LED (3) flashes green three times. Press the red star button to start recording. The LED (3) flashes one time. Press the START button (button 2) to add a highlight to your video. Press the ON button (button 1) to stop recording. The LED (3) flashes one time.

Using the camera

Recording is easy! Press the start button (again, the red star), the LED flashes red to show that the recording has started and the screen shows the recording time, if you have a HR monitor, you can switch screens to just look at your HR numbers.You can also start recording from the app, just press the record button after the camera is connected and that’s it. You can press the star button to create highlights.

Editing the videos *(on your computer) and on your phone.

If you download the Tom Tom Bandit studio from their site, you’ll be able to edit your videos and add overlays of speed/altitute/heart rate/etc very easily. You can also edit them with the app. Im working on a MAC and its super intuitive to make a full lenght video or instead a highlight one, adding overlays could not be easier but theres only one style of overlays, so there’s that. The camera creates MP4 files so you can use multiple other products to edit them. Again, if you have specific questions, please ask them on this review and I’ll answer them but dont want my review to get stale because I talk about features that can change.

Extra batteries:
If you find you need extra batteries, you can buy them for around $60 through the Tom Tom Site, I highly recommend you do this, I’ve noticed the battery life is a little less than 2 hours when 1080p 60, and I imagine cold temperatures will drop that.

Conclusion

All in all, the camera was ready to go in about 30 minutes from the moment I first opened the box. I had to update the firmware (to allow 4k recording), that was easy, inserted the memory card, created a MySports account through the App, definitively a very easy process and you don’t have to read instructions to figure it out if you are even remotely technical. The packaging is super cool and thats where I’ve decided to store the camera when not in use, well done Tom Tom. I’ve taken it on SEVERAL bike rides ranging from hanging out with the kids to I-shouldnt-be-doing-this-at-my-age downhill rides and it has performed w/o issues. To put it in perspective, I have two Yi 1080p cameras that only see storage now. I can’t wait for snow so that I can ski with this on!

I give it five stars because what it says it does, it does. I haven’t found flaws on it, would I like other features on it? Sure, an example of this is a screen that shows my speed when recording, that’d be cool..but I can’t dent the review on it because it doesnt have it, because it doesnt promise to have it.

Get it, you’ll love it, being able to edit videos on your phone or computer, add overlays on them, the image quality is top shelf, the audio recording is sufficient for extreme sports (I usually add music to the videos anyway...which the application allows you to do!).

I think I know every feature this camera has...if you have questions, comment on this review and I’ll be sure to help you out with questions.
