title: Blown Away! My 2700x  and XMP settings actually works out of the box?!
text:
This replaced a last gen Asus CH6... In short it was buggy from day one and remains so even now.(used all official and beta bio's versions) I spent hours tweaking and stabilizing the system and i was never quite satisfied with it. I was beginning to think the 2700x I have just wasn't a solid performer.

-ENTER x470 Gaming 7
Plugged up components,set xmp and system booted very quickly. (none of the memory training issues I was used to on the CH6..) Played a few game ran a few bench marks and the system was stable and temps were about 5c lower at the cpu despite 1.46v at max clock and full load.(check via thermal couple and true rms multi-meter.)

-Updating the Bios
Noticed board was on the f2 bio's so i updated to the latest f5 bio.(this was down from the bio's with the bio's flash tool) All went smoothly..

-Overclocking
Enabled precision boost overdrive and performed a slight over clock to memory and got into windows with cl18 3700mhz.. benched marked it. saved this profile.

Performed a low latency mem oc at cl14 3466mhz benched it and saved profile

Performed all core oc 4.4ghz w/ both memory settings ... all went well smoothly just
Settings used (these may not work for your cpu
1.bumped cpu vdd18 up until stable in all apps. ( 2.01 worked for me)
2.vcore to 1.39
3.soc1.1
4.cpu loadline turbo

- Conclusion
In about an 1hr and 30mins I think I got all I'm going to get out of the system. Could i push it higher with bclk and lots of voltage? Probably but this is good enough for me.

Overall I'm blown away by how well they system performs overall and the small intangibles like not waiting for 1-2mins for memory training or changes in bios actually working. The system is over all more responsive and boots 1000x faster. Gigabyte fan controls are some of the best I've used and it nice to be able to set water pump speeds. Though the stock setting speed profile work quite well.

Couldn't be happier just surprised that there was that much of a difference going from one motherboard to another with the same components! Never really experienced that much of difference in the last 10 years of building pc's.

- Additional thoughts
Only time will tell if the board will be well supported when the next gen of Ryzen comes out. Hopefully Gigabyte continues gives board the support it deserves!

title: Decent Compact Travel Headphones - Fair Sounding.
text:
I ordered these with high hopes. I ended up returning them. Here's what is right and wrong with them...

Pros:
They are compact. They fold up nicely, the cord is detachable and the included zippered pouch has room for an MP3 player or a spare battery for your phone. They sound decent for music. Listening to rock/metal, the guitars really stand out.

Cons:
They are muddy and lack mid-range. They do have plenty of bass, but a little too much for my taste. The bass drowns out the mid-ranges making dialogue on movies hard to hear. I wish they had an EQ button to turn on/off the bass boost. I also found I am not a fan of the on-ear style, I much prefer over-the -ear. After a 2 hour movie, you just want to take them off. They were fairly comfortable, and did isolate the outside noise nicely, but they just are not comfortable for long term wearing. The remote did nothing other than pause/un-pause playback on my Samsung Galaxy Note 4 and my wife's Note 3. No volume control, no track jumping, nothing. Very disappointed in that feature.

If you are wanting an OK, compact set of headphones for traveling then these might fit your bill. If you are just going to listen to music, these might be great for you. The price is right, but don't expect too much. They are definitely nicer than ear-buds, but there are better options out there. If you like lots of bass, then you will be happy with these. If you want to watch movies on a plane, find something else.

There are some comments about the build quality. I did find anything wrong with their construction. I feel that if you take care of them, they would last a long time. If you toss them in and out of a backpack without the pouch, then I could see some issues popping up over time. The rotating points seemed sturdy enough. The ear pads were well stitched and felt like they would hold up well. The padding on the top was an added bonus that I did not expect. The cord jack on the headphones has a nice 90-degree locking feature that will keep the cord from being yanked out accidentally.

title: Amazing sound! Don't let the size of these subs fool you!
text:
Don't let the size of these subs fool you. Granted you wont get the whumpa thumpa thunder booming subs you tend to hear low quality rap music on, but the sub really rounds your OEM sound out and provides some low end thump when rocking out in your car!

I bought two of these, wired them in parallel mono off of an LCQ-1 from Audio Control. I have a youtube video showing how I made one controller it comes with wired to work with two units simultaneously. To my knowledge I must be the first one to do this. I cannot post here but feel free to do a search. I can independently control both sub volumes relative to the door speakers/tweeters. Its very handy for various music samples as depending on the quality the bass frequencies are either too high or severly attenuated.

Using a frequency generator I see that the subs have very good SPL volume down to about 60HZ, below that the volume drops sharply. Anything lower than that you need some larger drivers to displace the air volume to really get the SPL's up.

Bottom line, highly recommended. I have two of them mounted on the floor of my 2015 Honda Fit EX 6MT USDM.

Compare this Zeiss Terra ED 8x25 to the world-class Swarovski 8x25 at $819 on Amazon (list price is even higher). This will show you

brightness (14.1 vs 14.2),

size in inches
b) specs favor Swaro: water resistant to 4 meters (vs 1 meter for Zeiss)
c) specs favor Zeiss: close focus 6.2ft (vs 14.2 for Swaro),
operating temperature -20 to 144˚ (vs -13 to 131 for Swaro)
d) use favors Swaro: view is said to be more comfortable to look at, ergonomically
focus has lighter touch, for those who like that
e) use favors Zeiss: view is more crisp, contrasty (Swaro view is said to be softer, more milky)
focus has firmer touch, for those who like that
f) price favors Zeiss: $293 (vs $819 for Swaro)

2. Compare them to other Zeiss binos from the SAME series - Zeiss Terra ED.
- 8x25, 10x25 are made in Japan
- 8x25, 10x25 are getting great reviews, for small binos
- all larger Terra ED models are made in China
- all larger models are getting panned for poor optics and build quality
I think everybody is well aware that China optics and build quality are inferior (so far) to those from the US, Japan, Taiwan, Germany, Austria, etc.

So this 8x25 model is unusual. Superior optics and build are normal for Zeiss, except for their Chinese built Terra ED line.
Luckily, the 8x25 model is made in Japan with Zeiss design. This results in typical world class Zeiss quality.

What is hard to understand is how Zeiss makes a $293 optic that arguably outperforms an $819 Swarovski.

For bino newbies looking at 10x25, remember: the 10x25 will have a smaller exit pupil, so your views may black out more. Also, a 10x is way harder to hold steady and actually see than an 8x. So, even though you think you want 10x, you probably really want 8x25. With the 8x25, you'll actually see and enjoy the view more.

title: Great 3D projector for gaming and movies.
text:
At the time of writing this I have owned and used this projector for just over 1 month. I have it hooked up via hdmi to my ps4 and pc, and use it to watch movies, and play games, both in 3d and otherwise. The projector is very bright. Colors and black levels are not as good as my 40" samsung, but I never expected them to be. There is a picture on this product's page that shows a simulated photo of normal, and eco mode. When compared side by side with my tv, the Normal image would more closely resemble this projector, and the SmartEco my tv. I do not list this as a negative, but a comparison to give any potential buyers an idea of what to expect. When wearing the 3D glasses, the color and black levels are significantly improved. Overall, the picture quality is every bit as good as what I see in theaters, and it can fill up to a 200" screen, something my samsung cannot do. I run this projector in Eco mode only, and it is located about 2 feet behind and to the left of my viewing position. The projector is quiet enough that it does not bother me, and when watching a movie or gaming I don't even notice it. Normal and SmartEco modes however, are a bit more audible.

Almost too insignificant to mention, is the fact that I can see a small amount of rainbow when viewing low resolution content, (SD streaming, netflix, amazon, etc.) if I am quickly looking from one side of the screen to the other. I only see this on bright white areas, such as subtitles, etc and I find it to be a very minor issue. I never see it when viewing 3d content, or while gaming. However, I am one of those who can see it easily, and I almost have to be looking for it to notice it.

For 3D I use Tridef and the EStar America ESG601 glasses mentioned by another reviewer. The glasses work perfectly, and the 3D is fantastic. Some of my games can appear washed out in 3D, and the tint, hue, etc cannot be adjusted on the projector when using hdmi connection. This is easily solved by using the settings for my video card. nVidia 3DTV Play is another option, but I find it too restrictive on resolutions and hz. With Tridef I can set it to top/bottom, and leave my resolution on 1080@60hz, which is far better than nVidia, which only allows 1080@24hz. I have noticed zero input lag in any mode or configuration, on either my ps4 or pc.

For an inexpensive screen I used RocLon blackout fabric from a local store. I tried both ivory, and white (which appeared gray to me) and the white in my opinion provided better colors and black levels.

title: Based on the great reviews, and my desire for future cord cutting
text: Based on the great reviews, and my desire for future cord cutting, I decided to give this antenna a try.  I purchased the 30 mile antenna, being 15 miles from Manhattan. I hooked it up to a 2nd floor TV and left the antenna standing upright behind the TV.  I ran a channel scan, and it showed 6 stations.  I assumed that these would be network stations. They were not. They were foreign language stations that didn't come in very well anyway.  I moved the antenna to another location and ran another scan. More stations this time, but only 1 of the 10 listed came in at all, and it was unwatchable, fading in and out, mostly just digital noise.  I tried everything, even ran the wire across the room so it was against a window. After an hour of moving the antenna to every possible point, having it vertical, horizontal, or a combination of both, I was unable to find ANY stations that were watchable.  I have no idea WHY these work so well for some, and so poorly for others.  I'm NOT the type of reviewer that would give a product 1 star because it was damaged in transit or any other reason other than the unit in question NOT functioning as designed and advertised.  I have no doubt that this may work perfectly well in some applications, but it gets 1 star because it does not function in MY application. This is the first time I have returned anything to Amazon, and fortunately, THAT process was quite painless.

title: Beautiful Replacement for Broken Headphone Jack!
text:
I purchased four sets of Sennheiser MX400 earphones for $4 a piece about eight years ago. They sound absolutely incredible, and I really like the type of earphones that hang in your ear, not the ones with silicone surrounds that you have to jam in your ears. When the headphone jack on my final pair started going out (gave all other pairs to friends / family), I was sad that I would lose my favorite pair of cheap earphones, as they are now discontinued, so I can't just buy another pair. The left channel would go out easily when the cable was bent around the jack, and sometimes both channels would go out.

I bought this repair kit to bring life back into my earphones, and the repair was easier than I thought it would be, thanks to Ray M. Bond's review, noting that you should tin the wire ends and headphone jack contacts before attempting to solder.

The only photo I didn't show is that I ended up putting small heat shrink over each contact inside the headphone jack before closing it up, which will not only prevent shorting, but it will also prevent the normal wear and tear that my headphones initially developed, necessitating this repair.

My repaired earphones look awesome, and this low profile jack will fit in any case I throw at it! When I plug into my lightning -> 3.5mm dongle, I get about 4 seconds of quiet clicking before the audio works perfectly (with iPhone 7), but with every other device I've tested, audio works perfectly immediately upon plugging in. I'll blame that one on Apple's dongle.

Very happy with this replacement, and will definitely buy another just to make my other headphones look classier!

title: An old classic, correctly reimagined
text:
I have always wanted a Polaroid Camera, and given that instant cameras are a trend again I decided to do a little research about them. I spent a few months comparing different models (the whole Fuji Instax line and the few that Polaroid was selling at the time) and I finally decided to buy this model (Polaroid Z2300).
After almost a year of owning this camera, I can clearly write about the pros and cons of owning this camera:

PROS:
-First of all, the fact that you can decide which photos you print is so underrated. You can not even imagine the number of times people appear with their eyes closed on the photograph.
-The design is really nice, it is a combination of the old-school, classic design and a modern, contemporary design. It is thicker than a normal digital camera but it is slick enough to put it in your pocket.
-You can edit your photos before you print them. It is really fun to take a photo and apply a black and white filter, or to accentuate the colors, for example.
-It has a lot of different modes, some more common than others (night, fisheye, fireworks, water, kids, party, among many others).
-The film is really cheap, in comparison to the Impossible Project. It is in the same price range as the whole Fuji Instax line but the film the Z2300 uses can also be used as a sticker.
-The build quality is good, it is completely made out of plastic. There is a wide variety of colors to choose from, I bought the white one, and despite all of the use, it is as clean as the first day I got it.
-The print quality is great, despite being a little grainy at times, but it depends on the photo you took. The film is just as Polaroid promotes it: you can touch it right after you printed it and the colors will not move, it resists a little water and it is said to be almost unbreakeable (I did not try this one myself because I did not want to risk losing a photo).

CONS:
-Despite the fact that the camera’s quality is 10mp, the photographs seem to be of less quality.
-I also bought the Neoprene Pouch and sometimes when I put the camera in it, the On/Off button turns on, so I have to put it in very gently.
-Since the film is also a sticker (as I mentioned earlier), after a few months the film starts to curve itself because of the glue it has, so that is one of the biggest letdowns in my opinion. The Fuji Instax does not have this problem because it is a little sturdier and more rigid.
-It does not have a counter to let you know how many papers you have left (like the old Polaroid cameras used to), so from time to time I have to open it (without letting the sun or any kind of light hit it directly so as to not ruin it) and check how many I have left.

Overall, it is a great camera and I recommend it, in spite of the film bending after a few months but it is just a minor setback. If you want to take photos and you are looking for an instant camera, it does not get much better than this.

title: PAPAGO GoSafe 118 - Fair Video Quality, Impressive Size and Features
text:
[[VIDEOID:89b3657f2747a2408191f18477ec3f0]] The PAPAGO GoSafe 118 was recently introduced to replace the previous GS-110 model. After a lot of research on the previous model, I decided on this model as my first dashcam due to the impressive features and small size at an entry-level price. After installing this earlier today, here's my preliminary review of the key features and usability of this dashcam. Note that you must purchase a MicroSD memory card Class 6 or above (8 GB to 32 GB) separately in order to use the dashcam at all.

The key advertised features of this dashcam are:
Video Resolution of 720p at 30 frames per second, 125° wide viewing angle
G-Sensor and Emergency Button
Automatic Turn-On
2" LCD Panel / Compact Size
Advanced: Stop & Go / Headlight Reminder / Driver Fatigue / Motion Detection
Advanced with Additional Purchase: GPS Location / Speed

A breakdown of each feature and my thoughts:

Video Resolution:
Provided with this review is a 30-second clip of the dashcam video performance at the maximum resolution of 720p at 30 frames per second, with the audio removed. The file was recorded in AVI format (not MOV as stated on their website) in a 3 minute clip, amounting to approximately 175 MB with audio. My thoughts on justifying this webcam was that 720p should be sufficient to record any incidents. However, the video quality makes me second guess on whether I should have sprung for 1080p. It is difficult to read license plate numbers unless you are stopped directly behind a car - even those of the vehicles in adjacent lanes are hard to make out. Note that this video has been edited to remove the audio, shorten the clip, and compress into an uploadable format - but I did my best to make sure that did not compromise this review.

G-Sensor and Emergency Button:
This feature ensures to write-protect a video clip in the event of any excessive vibration. Supposedly, even my installation triggered this, and I was pleased to find the video in a separate folder on the memory card. The emergency button allows one to write-protect the current clip manually. (The dashcam records in 3, 5, or 10 minute clips and overrides the oldest non-write-protected clips once the memory card is full). Because of the super capacitor on-board, the dashcam would be able to save the last video clip in the event of a sudden power loss.

Automatic Turn-On:
Since the dashcam is plugged into the cigarette lighter 12V port of the vehicle, there was no issue with it turning on and auto recording upon vehicle ignition. Unfortunately, for my vehicle it did not turn off automatically after exiting the car, but I'm not sure if I can blame this device as I have an electric car which may behave unconventionally.

LCD Panel and Compact Size / Installation:
The 2" LCD Panel is a great size and very clear easy and clear to use. I had originally anticipated for the dashcam to be hidden behind my rearview mirror, but unfortunately this provided an obstructed view given how my car's advanced electronics were implemented. The small size is impressive nevertheless. While the power cord is advertised to be able to be routed through the headliner, beneath your passenger floor mats and into your cigarette lighter 12 volt port, for my vehicle the cable came up a little short but I was able to make it by routing through the glovebox. Also be warned that the provided mount is a non-removable 3M sticker-mount, so be sure to experiment positioning in advance, and clean the glass before applying. The adhesive label can also be a bit difficult to remove.

Advanced Features:
The Stop & Go feature is great to provide a reminder beep after the car in front of you has moved in stopped traffic (e.g. at a traffic light), helping to avoid honks from those behind you. I did not use the auto headlight reminder as my vehicle automatically determines when to use headlights based on lighting levels, but it seemed to work properly on initial setup. The driver fatigue feature is simply to remind the driver to take a break after a set driving period (e.g. 2 hours), but I also disabled this given my primary use for commuting. Finally, the motion detection can be useful if you have the camera continuously powered and want video of when someone approaches your parked vehicle, but I disabled this (the default) given battery-draining concerns.

Additional Purchase Required - GPS Sensor:
Finally, there is an optional GPS sensor available for purchase for this dashcam, a feature I did not see available anywhere in this price range. Unfortunately, the sensor costs on the order of thirty bucks, but the ability to record your location and speed can be valuable evidence. I'll be looking into purchasing this add-on when I find it at a decent price, however the flexibility to upgrade is nice nevertheless.

Hope this helps. I'll try to update this review if I learn more or change my thoughts after more usage.

title: Does what it says
text:
I have computer speakers outputting audio from my television. However, the computer speakers don't have a volume remote and I used to have to get out of my seat to turn the volume up or down.

I bought this product to insert between the television and the computer speakers, and using long cables I placed it right where I sit to watch TV. Now I no longer have to get up to change the volume and it works great.

This item seems to work perfectly for my needs but there are 2 things I noticed. These things are non-issues for me. However, depending on how someone else plans on using this it may be important to know that..

1.) Sound still comes through when the volume is turned all the way down. It's VERY VERY faint, but if the input signal is loud enough you'll still be able to hear it when the volume knob is turned all the way down (especially if you're using headphones). There is no actual mute.

2.) The first 5% or so on this dial comes out as mono audio. Once you dial past 5% or so the sound comes through both sides.

Again these things are non-issues for me, and I imagine wouldn't bother most people. But depending on the set-up and use you have in mind you might care about this.

title: The old camera was really nice but had a weak mount that caused the camera ...
text:
Ubiquiti managed to improve their old airCam Bullet in every way they needed to. The old camera was really nice but had a weak mount that caused the camera (and video) to shake, had no IR support, and felt a bit on the cheap side of construction.

The new UVC has addressed all of these issues in spades. The camera housing is far more study with a nice retractable sun shade, and the mount is no longer flimsy PVC but metal with tension screws in each joint to really lock it in place. It now not only supports IR but includes IR illumination in-camera making this a really nice out door camera for moderate light conditions like outside of buildings or in dark rooms. They've even gone as far to include a microphone for audio recording, perfect for listening for warning beeps in distant, unmanned, equipment closets.

My complaints are very few and include some difficulty in aiming the camera. It's mount is rock solid but adjusting the multiple tension spots to get the camera just where you want it is difficult. I've dropped the small hex key they've included many times resulting in trips down a a ladder or down the stairs to retrieve it. I also wish the price point was slightly lower and closer to the old cameras $100-$120 mark opposed to this units $140. However I under stand the slight price increase with all the extras' they're providing.

Included are images from my front camera that keeps an eye our vehicles, one on a rainy night and one on a rainy afternoon.

title: Great headphones and Fantastic sound
text:
Firstly...I did not buy these from Amazon due to me getting them much cheaper elsewhere,,,However,this does not stop me from writing my review on these fantastic headphones....I'd just like to point out to those that are not familier with NC technology...Keeping things simple (it can get complicated) they work on counteracting (Mimic) the 'Constant' noise surrounding you and then elimintaing it and then letting the music you hear through.What some people think it does is eliminate Everything...this is not so...SO...if your listening to your music on a plane NC blocks out the constant drone...but if anyone should suddenly speak to you or make an announcement,you Will hear them because the sound was Not constant..After all...you don't want to be completly deaf to whats going on around you....Anyway onto my review.
I commute to the States regularly and on a 9+ hour flight the drone of aircraft noise often spoilt my listening pleasure of my music and watching on board movies...I'd seen others using the Bose and Sennheiser but when I saw the price of them I thought 'No way'...AKG have done equal if not better at a much lower cost..and you won't be dissapointed...These sound wonderful on their own without even turning the NC on...The clarity and soundstage is top notch...the bass is tight and even (not to big and not too small)...midrange and treble is nice and crisp...they have a nice open sound....I listen to Jazz,but also listen to pop and rock...to be honest I listen to whatever takes my fancy on a journey,but going back to the Jazz side...the soundstage is great...you can pick out where the instruments were placed with ease and the bass lines suited Jazz perfectly...Pop gets the same treatment and they can rock with the best out there......Turn on the NC in a noisy enviroment and WOW...no more disturbance...you hear the music nice and clear...the background noise simply dissapears...no more plane drone or train rattle...Very impressive.

The headphones themselves are very well made...top notch...and they are very very comfortable for On the ear phones...I suffer with my ears getting hot usually when wearing any type of phones..but not with these..even after several hours I experienced no over heating or uncomfortable pressure build up..The trim of the phones are aluminium and the open mesh area on the cans themselves are exactely as the photo shows....certainly not shiny as someone has mentioned...Someone also mentioned about them being quiet and I can only imgaine they were using a not so good music source...I've also used these headphones with my Fiio Amp/Dac and what a difference it makes...more power and more authority across the music range.The phones come with a dedicated usb power lead for charging the inbuilt NC battery which does last a good 30 hours (well they have for me)..What happens after the battery gives up will still leave you with some top notch well sounding headphones,but this should be a long time away...The case is a neoprene snug fit zipped bag with just enough room to place the leads in also...just be careful not to loose the power lead as it can cost about $40/50...although I cannot even find where to get one anyway...so it looks like being very careful with the one that was supplied..

To wrap up...I really can't fault the phones themselves...Fantastic sound...Great quality and impressive Noise cancelling ...Highly Recomended.

title: This graphics card is amazing. It's probably not THE top of the line ...
text:
This graphics card is amazing. It's probably not THE top of the line as of this current date, but it enables you to taking your gaming to a higher level. I emulate a lot of PlayStation 2 games and having this graphics card granted me the luxury of reliving all of my favorite games in glorious 1080p HD 3x native resolution. It's almost like you're playing them for the first time if your settings are all optimized.

The ONLY issue I had with this graphics card is that my computer now has to behave differently. My desktop is a Gateway DX4870, and even though I have installed the card properly and everything, for some reason I can't just turn on my computer and expect it to boot normally. If I just press the power key and wait for it to boot up, it gets stuck at a black screen and nothing happens. I thought that the problem might be my power supply, but it's sufficient enough for the card which was the whole reason I bought this version over the overclocked card. In order for me to ACTUALLY boot my PC into Windows, I have to press the "ESC" key six or so times rapidly as SOON as I see the Gateway logo appear, and then it will change to Ameritech or something like that. After my desktop beeps a few times within a minute or so, my PC will finally boot into Windows. It's very strange but I have a feeling it isn't exactly the graphic card's fault.

Because the graphics card works so phenomenally, I don't mind having to press the ESC key a bunch of times every time I turn on my computer. Not only can I emulate PS2, GameCube, and Wii games beautifully, but I can pretty much max out the settings on almost any game on Steam. Dead Island, Garry's Mod, DreadOut, Left 4 Dead 2, etc. All of them run without virtually any hassle.

I definitely recommend this card but BEWARE of the fact that your computer might not like it inside of it at first. If your desktop gets stuck on a black screen at startup like mine, just power it on again and mash the "ESC" key a bunch of times as soon as you see your desktop manufacturer's name and logo until it changes to something else. I hope this helps someone else!

title: Definitely has potential, but definitely not good enough just yet
text:
Overall, I do like this abcGoodefg Wireless Handheld In-Air Mouse, but because of the price and a few issues I have with it, I can only rate it at 2.5 stars at the most.

I do like the overall design of the locations of the trackball, the scroll wheel, and the button, but I feel that they are all too hard to use fluently. With the trackball, I feel that it is too sensitive even at the lower dpi option, and I found it very hard to get the cursor to go precisely where I want it to with the mouse being comfortably held. It is also hard to properly control the trackball if the mouse is not in an upright position, so it cannot be held sideways and still function, something that I was looking forward to be able to do. While holding the mouse with my thumb on the trackball and my index finger and middle finger on the top and bottom buttons, respectively, I find it pretty hard to press on the buttons. It doesn't feel too bad initially, but I cannot imagine myself having to use this mouse over a long period of time or having to constantly click the buttons even for a few rapid times in a row.

The material of this mouse also feels somewhat cheap. It is nice that the mouse is lightweight because it is an in-air handheld mouse so I believe this aspect is very important, but this mouse does not feel like it is purposely constructed to be lightweight but more like it is lightweight because of lower quality material being used.

I was really hoping that I would want to use this mouse almost on a daily basis, but after trying it out for a few times, I have left it in its box ever since. I am disappointed with this mouse as it pertains to the user experience, and I believe it is priced way too high with regards to the flaws I have mentioned. Personally, I would not purchase this mouse even at $15 or so because I cannot find myself wanting to use it. However, I do think that this mouse has great potential, and if the company can make it much more pleasant to use, then it will easily be worth its current price of around $40 or so. With this current product at its current price, I can only rate it at 2 to 2.5 stars.

title: A Boon Indeed & Yes, The Storage Space is All There (See Notes)
text:
PROS:
+ Sleek and polished design
+ Compact (when you consider that it’s a desktop drive) and can be seated vertically or horizontally
+ 7200rpm spindle, verified with CrystalDiskInfo (it’s not often that you come across a true 7200rpm external hdd, at least not without paying a pretty penny for it)
+ Whisper quiet even when awake and active
+ Conserves energy by going to sleep after ~15 minutes of inactivity and wakes promptly when accessed

NEUTRALS:
* The plug is unusual in that it needs to be assembled, sort of. It comes in two separate pieces and you must slide the prongs into the sleeve until it clicks. Very simple and takes two seconds...it’s just annoying because the instructions don’t specify this.

CONS:
- No internal fan--that said, even when transferring 2TB of data, including several files 2GB+, the drive didn’t overheat in the least...still, a fan would provide some added peace of mind
- The plug isn't space-saving in the least--in fact, if you're using a standard strip it will take up 2-3 sockets (one for its prongs, its body covers the second, and the cord--though flexible--takes up another)

Rarely do I rate items 5 stars, but this drive deserves it. I originally purchased this 4TB drive to replace a failing Seagate Expansion. In my search for a new drive, I opted for this because it sported a 7200 rpm spindle, USB 3, the price was right, and Toshiba is a name I trust. I ended up liking this drive so much that I put it into my daily rotation rather than relegate it to blue-moon storage.

NOTES:
* Since I use my own backup software, I can’t speak to the ease of use, stability, or reliability of the included backup software. Nor can I speak to use with Mac. I tested it briefly with my Xbox and it was easily recognized without issue.

* Another reviewer mentioned only receiving 2TB of the 5TB listed on his drive. I wanted to clarify that his disk may have arrived with a partition. When my first drive arrived and I loaded it up, it said I only had 1TB of usable space. Of course, I was fuming and ready to ship it back, but I wanted to fully check out the drive first. I opened up disk manager and saw that the drive was partitioned leaving 1TB allocated and formatted with the remaining 3TB unallocated. It was odd the drive would arrive with only one usable partition, but I shrugged, deleted the partition, allocated, and reformatted the drive--problem solved.

In the six months that I’ve been using this drive (the first drive is in a constant state of being on since it's functioning as a lightweight media server), I’ve not had a single problem with it. In fact, I just purchased a second one to use as my primary backup drive. However, should anything change with either drive, I will update my review accordingly. If you have any questions about this drive or my experience with it, leave a comment and I’ll do my best to answer.

title: Quality and more from an extension cable
text:
How can an audio cable extension get a five-star review? Easy. With all the horrible competition out there they came in above all expectations in a multitude of metrics.

First, the wire gauge is large enough to carry the signal. Some may think that should be a given, but it is not (and you know it). The wiring is heavy and the insulation is thick and stiff. I anticipate many years' use from this cable.

Secondly, the connectors are metal (obviously with insulation), well-made, and feel very sturdy. Like the wiring, this is high-quality material. It connects with a tactile "snap" and I know it won't come loose unless I want it to come loose.I'm connecting a headset-with-microphone across a room and any of the above could compromise the quality coming to me or going out. I've been told there's no loss of signal when I use this cord.

The product was shipped promptly and the company inquired quickly after it was delivered, wanting to confirm that it arrived in good shape and on-time.

I like this company so much I'm specifically looking for their name when I next buy some sync cables for my iPhone (and an auto charger for the same). Sometimes a company takes their jobs and products seriously. This is the first one I've seen in a long time. I'm surprised I can still get this kind of quality in a modern world where everything (else) is built to break.

They've earned some loyalty from me in my first purchase.

title: Security with GoControl and Wink Hub 2
text:
Just installed yesterday so there's not too much to say so far. Using it with a Wink Hub 2 and setup and pairing was a breeze. The motion detector also reports on room temperature. There have been complaints about the lack of hanging hardware for the motion sensor - basically, you can hang in on a screw in the wall, or use the included two-sided adhesive pad. The only problem with the pad is, once it's stuck on the wall, it's stuck there. I decided to use 3M Command tape - a sort of mounting tape with removable adhesive on one side, and a velcro type texture on the other. That way, when the battery runs out, or you decide to move the sensor someplace else, no problems with wall marks.

The door sensors work well and were easily mounted with adhesive tape included (they have a removeable top, so changing the battery shouldn't require taking the whole sensor off the wall. Using Wink Hub 2's "Robots", I can easily schedule on times when I wlll get an instant text or email if a door is opened, or someone is detected inside the house. So far, it has worked flawlessly. title: The best accessory for a phone

From what I read about the Apple Watch, its most important feature are its alerts of incoming calls, texts, etc. Well, the Ditto does exactly the same for a fraction of the cost. I wear the Ditto clipped to the inside of my shirt below my neckline. It vibrates enough to be noticed, but so much to be indiscreet. My biggest problem with it? Anyway now I can play (WOT) World of Tanks at over 100fps using almost the highest settings. The new maps in Patch 1.0 look amazing with this card. I plan on loading more games once I find my Steam password again. However I am pleased even though this is not a barn burner video card it plays many games perfectly fine even though you might not be able to play them at maximum video settings. I hope this holds out until the prices of video cards come down. its sad what is happening right now in the video card world! title: Kind of mostly good, but could be better
text:
Okay so I got this because Google Cast isn't the best at screen mirroring. My Internet isn't the greatest and since all this is through WiFi there is often bad lagging or audio mishaps. So I figured why not, I have an S6 and a Tab A from Samsung, surely their piece of kit works better, right?

Kind of mostly, but sort of not really.

So it JUST does screen mirroring, which is awesome and useful, but for 35 and a Chrome Cast I get apps I can directly cast to my TV. The screen mirroring for all intents and purposes is just a bonus perk. But still, I can actually CHANGE SETTINGS through a dedicated app on the Chrome Cast. You don't get that option here and it's actually making me very mad. I have very little control of this thing.

Another issue is that It's just on all the time, and it gets very hot to the touch just idling all day. It turns into a miniature furnace when you're actually using it: there's not a single vent hole on this thing.There's no auto shutoff, there's no power button. You just unplug it and plug it back in (or use the USB port in your TV to power it which turns it off when the TV is off, but I only have the 1 usb port and thats for my Chromecast).

Like I said earlier there is no real way to control this thing from your device. I'm currently having an issue where the "dongle" won't update on my Tab A, but somehow it updated when I connected my S6? Okay so wait, is my DEVICE updating, or is the dongle?! Because it straight up says dongle firmware, not "debice". Apparently it's my phone's Allshare software (again, I have no control over this, it just has a barebone connect option, no settings, no update, nothing) and it will let me cast from my phone now, but the update refuses to install via my tablet. So then I'm like okay fine, Google it. Only there's no answers there. So then I say okay fine screw it, I'll just proceed without the update. NOPE! It just crashes on my tablet without the update now.

When it works it works great, much better than my Chromecast as far as screen mirroring is concerned. But due to the heat it will freeze and die after a few hours, then you have to pull the plug and let it sit and cool off for a while.

So for 50 bucks I have a piece of equipment that replaced a MUCH better micro usb to HDMI option that was cheaper and DIDN'T rely on fickle wireless (oh imagine that the new Samsung devices don't support the cable option anymore). But there's no app to control any settings, or updates, or power settings. There's no standby mode or an off switch for the thermonuclear device: not a single vent hole. It also doesn't treat any of my devices equally like my Chromecast does (which even works with my Note 10.1 (2012).

So I don't know. Its kind of an okay buy, but I expect ACTUAL functionality and options out of stuff like this these days. I mean come on, no app?! A hole or two in the case?!

I never used to be a real fan of wearing over the ear headphones, but now I am! I usually just wear earbuds, I did purchase some other BOSE headphones and now I have the QC35s! I was blown away on how when you put them on, turn the switch to ON, the world fades away! These headphones have an amazing punch (bass) at both high and low volumes. Everything sounds clear and like how it was intended to be heard and I think that because of also the noise cancelling technology. The headphones are of a higher quality, the ear cushions feel great on your ears for hours. There is also a nice cushion for the top of your head. The buttons don't feel like they're going to break off, but they are placed in a great spot, I can pause, play, FF/RW songs, AND even talk to Siri!

The battery life is amazing, they come with an initial 50-60% charge and even after hours of listening it takes a while for the battery to deplete as I barley had to charge them up after a week and a half use.

As for the packaging, they come in nice, small and compact case. I am very impressed with the case as my other headphones the case is too large, these headphones fold up nicely into the case which I feel I can tuck nicely into my backpack. In the case comes a wire for a wired connection (if you choose), the airline adapter and a USB charging cable. The bad thing with the charging cable is that it is a little short and does not come with a charging block.

Overall I am in love with these headphones and I strongly feel BOSE did a great job engineering/ designing these.

title: Life in the Convergence Zone
text:
The Kayo Maxtar K2 is one powerful device as well as a near-essential for life in the convergence zone where the weather is always unpredictable during the Fall and Winter months. "Expect the unexpected" and you will never be disappointed.. Preparation is everything.. Each year about this time we restock batteries, check lanterns and flashlights, test our generator, make certain our potable water containers are handy, and check off myriad other tasks that by now have become our seasonal routine.

New to us this year is the Kayo Maxtar K2. With its 4 USB ports, a 12v as well as a 20v port, and its 50,000 mAh the K2 is an elegant and beautifully designed device. We can easily keep 4 phones charged and ready-to-go wherever we are -- however remote.

The K2 is no lightweight however, and I've found that it fits perfectly in the front zippered pocket of my trusty Victorinox daypack, a pack that I take nearly everywhere -- whether out in the back pastures of our sheep farm or tucked behind the driver's seat whilst out and about or stowed along with our family's other packs and carry-alls while on a longer trip across the mountains and high-desert. All the places where we will be glad to have the K2 so charging capabilities are with us wherever we are. Peace of mind, in other words.

I have not yet used the other ports, but know we will. I was pleased to learn that a K3 is in the works that sounds as though it will be just the thing to keep our various MacBooks, MacBook Pros, and iPad chugging along just as easily as the K2 handles our iPhones.

I've found customer service from Kayo Maxtar to be beyond exceptional. The day before our K2 was scheduled to arrive I received an email from Zola asking me to please let him know when our package arrived to reassure him that it was indeed the device we'd ordered. When our package arrived the following day, I opened it promptly and was able to reassure Zola that all was as it should be and that the K2 and all its accessories where safely tucked inside. That night I tested the K2 by charging all our phones and found that the device performed perfectly.

Zola has been phenomenal, checking back with me regularly to be sure we are happy with our K2 as well as answering several technical questions I had regarding whether or not the K2's 12v would be capable of powering my Hansen e-Spinner (a beautifully-crafted portable spinning wheel). After checking with his technical team, it seems as though the K2 is not a good choice for this purpose.

But in terms of keeping our phones charged at all times, regardless of power outages and other inconveniences that no doubt lay in wait during the Fall and Winter months to come, I have no doubt whatsoever that our family is in great hands with the K2.

title: The Best value on the Market
text:
This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.

title: Super fast (at distruction)
text:
I bought the SM951 because it offers read and write performance that is incredible.

As a basis for comparison, I used CrystalDiskMark to compare it to the [[ASIN:B00CKAOJA0 Seagate 600 SSD]] I have as my main boot disk, a and RamDisk (DDR3 1600). The results are rather impressive when compared side by side.

Samsung SM951
Sequential [MB/s]: 1253 Read / 1229 Write

RamDisk (DDR3 1600)
Sequential [MB/s]: 3283 Read / 4765 Write

Seagate SSD
Sequential [MB/s]: 464.9 Read / 391.5 Write

Note that a RamDisk is really just a driver that enables me to use my computers memory like a disk. It's naturally faster, but does rely on an HDD to persist data, so I don't recommend using one for actual storage, but they are handy if you need to perform fast reads/writes .

Now for the reason for the 1 star rating:
The problem is that I had installed my programs, and started using the drive for video remuxing. I came home yesterday, and all my source video's were gone, complete loss, nothing in the recycle bin, and the application logs on the same drive also gone.

title: Excellent tablet, performs very well for me!. After 2 years, I am still very happy with this tablet. Detailed review follows...
text:
Updated review June 26, 2017
Well, I have owned this tablet for over TWO YEARS and it auto updated to Marshmallow in late April, 2017. It still charges to 100 percent, and still runs perfectly. Since I have had this tablet close to the first day it came out and I really am pleased with it, even more so now (June 26, 2017). When I purchased it, I was looking for a 9.7 size and a tablet that would do what I wanted a nice and useful tablet yet not the most pricey one out there. Hence, I bought this Tab A 9.7 and am so pleased with it. The purpose of this review is to hopefully help you decide if this tablet is the right one for you or not... Below are the PROS and the CONS that I found after testing this tablet:
Also, after purchasing a new HP wireless printer and installing 3 apps from Playstore, I print directly from this tablet over WiFi...see info in comments.

PROS/SPECIAL FEATURES:

+ Size - I had the Tab 4 10.1 and the 8.0 before this tablet. The 10.1 was just too large and bulky and heavy. This tablet is lighter than my old Tab 4 10.1 and more comfortable to hold and to carry in my purse or backpack.

Screen Resolution, Brightness and Other Info – Yes, the resolution on this screen is not the highest one out there, yet I find the display clear and easy to view, read eBooks, etc. So. But do not let the resolution scare you away because the screen is clear and the colors are so vivid, they just pop with color! And I find it easy to read eBooks, watch videos, etc on this tablet. For the price of this tablet, I find that the tablet has been a great purchase because after 6 months of using it every day, I am still very happy with it. There are other tablets out there that are much pricier as Tab S2 a d now the Tab S3, but for me, I shall keep this one!

* The screen aspect ratio is 4:3 vs the 16:1 type of screen. For me, I like this 4:3 screen because I found that the webpages are easier to read and clearer, I did not have to scroll to the right. Also I found that the pictures on a website were easier to view. I compared this tablet with my older Tab 4 10.1 tablet on my frequent webpages and while I viewed this tablet, I could read the larger text better, read my eBooks much clearer, emails better etc. This is my personal discovery from my testing of this and comparing it to my older tablet.

+ Battery life/Speed – Very good battery life! For me, I have found that I am constantly on WiFi (Internet). However, I also find that this tablet gets me 2 to 3 hours MORE daily than my older Tab 4 10.1 did! Even after over two years of ownership, I am experiencing excellent battery life.
The tablet I find is quite responsive and peppy with no lagging. The Lollipop runs this tablet wonderfully.

+ WiFi Connecting/Speed of WiFi and MORE - This tablet connects SUPER quickly to my home WiFi and has never ever dropped the WIFi signal no matter where I am in my home. WiFi is VERY STRONG using this device, even when I am very far from my router I still have 4.5 bars! *** To test the speed and strength of this WiFi and compare it to my other Android devices, I went to the Playstore and got the free app called WiFi Analyzer. This is a MUST HAVE app for any Android device as it gives you a visual report on the WiFi strength of your tablet, phone etc.

+ SPECIAL INFO about INTERNET CONNECTION - Yes, this is a WiFi only, but when you are away from an WiFi internet hotspot location, there are ways to can get onto the internet such as MiFi and there are ways that you can purchase equipment so that you can have data when you do not have a WiFi hotspot available.

+ Internet & Webpage & Video Viewing - The stock browser does a wonderful job and it opens up webpages very fast. Also I tried Maxthon Browser and this worked very well yet I still prefer the Internet App. Also, I tried out the factory installed Chrome Browser and liked it OK, yet again, I went back the the stock Internet App (this is my preference). Note that the Playstore has many very good (FREE) internet browsers as Dolphin, Opera and many more!

+ EXTERNAL SLOT FOR MICRO SD CARD. This is a must for me as I keep my personal files, photos, and music on my internal SD card. I installed a SanDisk 32GB SD card and it works great on this tablet and I placed my music and files on it and have plenty of space left.

- + Camera / Video Camera - I found it OK for a 5MP with no flash on this camera, however, in good lighting the pictures came out better had I expected. However, I rarely use this camera as I prefer to use my Nikon digital camera for my overall picture taking...the camera on this tablet is OK for backup camera, taking pictures to send in an email, etc). Do not expect the camera on this tablet to replace your digital camera since it does not have a flash and 5MP is rather low by todays standards.

+ Home Videos - The stock video player is OK and plays MOST home videos, however, may I suggest QQ Player (Free App from Playstore and the ONLY one I recommend as it plays every home video I tried).

+ Music Player/Sound Quality - This model has the regular MUSIC App, which plays by playlists, songs, albums and even folders. Also there is Google Music app is pre-installed in this tablet and does a fine job. However, I installed the FREE app called Rocket Player from the Playstore and love this music player! As for sound quality - The best way to really enjoy music is through a high quality Bluetooth speaker or Bluetooth headset as the sound quality is superb this way and you can walk about your home listening to your music!

+ OTG USB Compatible - This tablet comes with a free OTG On the Go adapter cable. Just plug in your flash drive and you can copy files to the flash drive so easily or view files that are on the flash drive. *Note that portable external hard drives and portable DVD/CD drives will not work using OTG in this tablet because they require a lot of power.

CONS:
- Just ONE CON - Wish that the resolution were higher...however I am very happy with the display's colors and readability etc (see pictures).This is the only con I could find personally. However, as I stated above, this is not a deal breaker for me as I find the screen adequate.

Bottom line- The price is OK (not cheap) and it is the PERFECT SIZE, LIGHTWEIGHT TO HOLD and I am very happy with the tablet overall as it is peppy, colors vivid and this is a great tablet for reading and internet, etc.
However, for me, I really am enjoying this tablet and my true score is 4.4 stars because of the resolution..

Bottom line and my true rating is 4.3 stars (rounded off to 4 stars) because of the resolution. However, if you are looking for a tablet with lots of features and Samsung quality, and do not have to have the very highest resolution, then highly consider this excellent tablet!

title: Sennheiser did it again... and better
text:
In the past 5 years I have been the happy owner of the RS 180. When the RS 185 came out, it seemed like a logical upgrade to me so I went ahead and ordered them.

My initial feeling was a bit of a disappointment as the RS 185 sounded like they had very weak bass compared to the RS 180. The highs were so overwhelming that they actually disturbed me when watching TV in the first hour or so. Now we're a week later (about 10 hours of use) and while the RS 185 are still not fully broken in, I must say they sound great. The bass are good (although I'd like a bit more of them) and the sound is so much clearer than on the RS 180 that I wouldn't want to go back. If you buy the RS 185, make sure you break them in before judging them. When coming out of the box they were impossible to compare to my RS 180 that had over 2000 hours of use.

Here is a quick comparison of the RS 185 vs. the RS 180:

Good:
- The sound is much clearer with much better separation. It is so good that you can tell when your source is badly recorded (e.g. some TV shows). Now I feel that my RS 180 sound "messy" comparatively.
- Thanks to the digital connection, there is virtually no background noise
- The cups are a little bigger than on the RS 180, which is nice if you have bigger ears
- The extension of the headband is a lot smoother than on the RS 180
- The power button and the volume buttons are much more usable as their placement is better and the volume buttons are bigger
- The headphones green power LED has been placed on the back, it's not too bright and it doesn't blink (this was sometimes disturbing on the RS 180)
- The base station now has an auto-on. Only the headphones have to be turned on manually.
- The range of the RS 185 is slightly better than the RS 180 but nothing to write home about. I was expecting a bigger difference. Note that I only tested the penetration through walls and not in line of sight.
- The perceived quality of the materials used is slightly better than the RS 180 but they're not made of gold either

Neutral:
- The RS 185 have a pretty tight fit on the head which is good because they won't move but it makes them slightly less comfortable than my old RS 180. They may loosen up with time though.

Room for improvement:

title: The easiest way for me was to park both vehicles on a flat surface at a comfortable difference between the rear with the camera and the ...
text:
First the instructions are very basic and a joke.

Be prepared to have to dig out a wiring diagram unless you have a dual bulb dual wire system. My 2007 Dodge grand caravan uses a wire harness with an integrated housing. This meant I had to dig out a wire diagram or my continuity tester to figure out what wire to splice into. Second wireless is not truly wireless. You have to wire power to the camera and to the transmitter which means you can spend as much time routing wires as a wired system.
T
he biggest thing is just a note of caution. Just because you have everything up and running doesn't mean your done. You need to adjust the camera and angle and calibrate the parking lines if you use them. The easiest way for me was to park both vehicles on a flat surface at a comfortable difference between the rear with the camera and the front of the other car. Then adjust the camera angle till the red or yellow line (as you choose) lines up on the bumper. Since I have a young inexperienced driver I opted to leave more room than my other cars that came with backup OEM cameras.

The display is good but does get washed out in bright light as does the camera. At night there seems to be enough light but I would love to see IR led's in place of white light LED's instead. Another plus for the display is it has a usb port so you don't lose a power source using the display.

title: Just use your phone
text:
As a long time Garmin fan, I'm very underwhelmed by this product. It has some slick features but the reliability is disappointing. I've had this long enough to give a legit review. Unfortunately, long enough that it's not eligible for returns. Some issues I have with this:

- If you want traffic you'll need to activate the app on your phone or buy an additional adapter. So now instead of just using my phone for traffic and nav, I can turn on this device, find my destination, open up my phone, activate the app, hope it connects to the device remotely (which doesn't always happen), and then wait minutes for it to upload traffic information. Your phone can do all that in seconds.

- Occasionally on power up, none of the buttons work so I have to power down and start back up.

- I've been driving down the road when suddenly it activates voice control, wanting me to speak commands to it. But when I want to activate voice control I can never get it to work.

- The lane guidance has come in handy, but also has told me to be in the wrong lanes causing me to miss my exit ("be in second lane from left" yet it's only the left lane that exits the highway)

- It has tried to send me down one way streets which is a problem I never had with my old Garmin.

- I do like when it says things like "Turn right at the starbucks", but being in the city I've also received directions like "Turn right at XYZ tower" when I have no idea what sky scraper is the XYZ tower.

I'm giving it two stars because if it's your first nav you might like it, and I do like how traffic tells me the length of the delay / counts down the mileage until I'm out of the traffic jam. But ultimately I say just use an app on your phone.

text:
I bought this turntable prior to knowing its issues with footfalls. Luckily, I have never had problems with it (I’ve lived on the second floor in two places with it). When it works it is a beautiful sounding turntable. Super detailed, has a ton of punch. I love the thing.

Still I would take what other reviewers have said into consideration. I am lucky that the places I’ve lived have had sturdy floors.

A solution that seems to solve the footfall problem is to upgrade the tonearm to a satisfy tonearm at the front end of purchase. Everything I have read states this gets rid of the footfall problems and is an excellent tonearm (my clearaudio is equipped with the stock verify tonearm as I have never needed to upgrade it. If you get this I would consider getting the satisfy up front because it comes at a large discount if you buy it at the same time as the turntable).

Another thing I would say is the setup for this turntable is fussy. I would only recommend getting this if you have a dealer near by that you trust to help you with the setup.

If you are considering buying this be very up front and express your concerns to your dealer, see if you can work something out if there are problems.

All of these things certainly make this turntable not for everyone, but if you get it right it’s a fabulous sounding piece of equipment.

title: A Very Nice Little Machine
text:
I bought this because trying to use my Nexxus tablet to browse the Web was a nightmare, even after a full factory reset.

PROS
- While sitting on a recliner, the machine works great ergonomically.
- Features a fully featured version of Chrome and Google Apps, not the dumbed down, functional but annoying Android versions. Chrome on the Chromebook fully mirrors Chrome on my two desktops.
- It has enough capacity to run Chrome and Webapps without any major issues. A little slower than a desktop maybe but not terribly so.
- Very light weight.

IT IS WHAT IT IS
- the keyboard is functional. It's a little smaller than I'd prefer but that's an expected trade-off.

CON
- There is no option for a simplified waking password. You need to type in your real Google password anytime you to wake it up. Mine is quite involved so it's involved every time. You can set it so your phone unlocks when nearby but that doesn't always work. With a lot of flutzing, you can get your cell phone to sort of unlock it... sometimes. Though maybe it's my iffy Huawei phone.

TIPS
Once the updates downloaded and I rebooted the machine, it was fully functional. Stuff like Android Play store and phone unlocking wouldn't work until I rebooted after the updates.

Google how to use a Chrome mousepad. Knowing how and when to use two and three fingers really makes Web browsing much easier. You can even right click to pin tabs (Gmail, Calendar, etc) you want to keep up permanently.

OVERALL
This a great value for the money. I am extremely pleased. Easily the best of this sort of thing that I have ever owned.

UPDATE
I still LOVE this machine. And now it's even $30 cheaper than when I bought it.

Yesterday I installed the Linux version of Blender for a night class. It took some hacking skills but eventually I got it running. Though once installed, it wasn't the best experience; I had to reboot a few times, but it was much better than I expected. I'll use my real computer for all my Blend-ing outside of class. But Blender running pretty good on a $200 machine!

title: so I would only recommend it for light duty use
text:
This is a very well made light duty boom! I use this for a hair light and for some back lighting depending on the situation, and it works excellently. I only use it with a small-medium soft box and a speedlight using an S-type mount and it works well for that. This setup does seem to be on the verge of it's abilities with this setup at max extension however, so I would only recommend it for light duty use. As far as the stand quality itself, this is the best stand I own as far as feel (and I have several other Manfrotto compact stands). The release and tensioning mechanisms have a really solid feel, and I love the friction bars top and bottom for moving and securing the legs into position. Both the legs and primary bar have plenty of thickness and heft to them, that I don't expect them to give out for any reason. The only weak spot on this frame is the final extension tube is fairly small and thin, and does flex some even with my light weight setup when making adjustments.

I would highly recommend this for light duty use, but I'm not sure it would hold up to heavy mono-lights in a studio. I would definitely look elsewhere for any heavier lighting combos. I imagine this boom will last me for many years to come from it's build quality though! I did opt for iron weights instead of sand for various reasons including wear. If you're into portability there are some great water bladder weight options as well!

note: I noticed some reviewers mentioned the adjustment handle was missing from the boom, mine did arrive with this item just fine, and everything was in the package needed for setup.

title: Poor components quality for the price and poor warranty support
text:
Less than one year ago I bought this HT-ST7 Sony sound bar, which is one of the most expensive model of the Sony sound bar family.

Recently, I noticed an annoying distortion coming from its subwoofer while reproducing specific bass frequencies, such as movie explosions, videogame shooting and jazz music bass. After talking to Sony Customer Service, I received the authorization to submit my device for repair under its 1-year warranty.

After spending $50 to pack my device, I shipped it to United Radio, the company based in New York in charge of repairing Sony electronic in US (yes, regardless where you live, you will have to ship your defective product to New York). They received my sound bar and the initial diagnostic was there wasn't any problem with it. I sent e-mails to their customer service detailing the problem and offering options to reproduce the issue I found, which I believe they ignored. They decided there wasn't any problem and returned my sound bar which I just received and verified the annoying distortion keeps coming from the subwoofer speakers.

Based on my experience with subwoofers and home theaters, usually the source of this kind of problem is the subwoofer components, such as the spider or its cone, and I specifically ask United Radio check those components. Now that I had my sound bar returned with "no problems", I decided to investigate the problem further and found there were 3 HOLES (!!!) in the spider of the subwoofer speaker (the yellow membrane of the speaker) which is causing the distortion, which you can sse in the attached photo.

Now I'll have to start a battle against Sony to have my sound bar fixed, but if I could regret, I wouldn't pay the $1.300 I paid for this product. How could three holes appear in the speaker membrane in less than 1 year of use?

title: THIS is what you should buy for your Panasonic camera.
text:

Very good quality, as far as I can tell from some brief testing. As good as OEM Canon and Nikon wired shutter releases that I own for those brands of cameras, only much less expensive.

I don't know why the Panasonic "brand" (OEM) remote release is priced as high (over US $40!) as it is. Canon/Nikons are nowhere near as expensive.

But back to this particular item...

The rubber covering on the actual wires is substantially thicker than the "Foto-Tech" equivalent product that I got a few days ago, and unlike the Foto-Tech product, this Neewer item has a larger "body" to house the shutter button, and the button itself - again, unlike the Foto-Tech - provides for good pressure feedback so that one can tell, first, when one is making the camera focus, and then, when one is taking the shot.

See my review of the Foto-Tech product, which I found completely disappointing, but not worth returning,

You'll be happy with this (Neewer) item.

title: Just "ok"
text:
The detection range and sensitivity is the real problem with these cameras.

Detection range is listed at 20 feet. That's pretty mediocre honestly and I've found it to be more like 10-15 feet in actual use. Fine if you want to use in a doorway area or right over your driveway, but if you want to cover your entire back yard or any larger area, it just doesn't catch what you want it to.

Sensitivity is also an odd setting. You can turn it up to 6-9 and get an alert every time a leaf falls, tree blows in the wind, car drives by out of frame, etc or turn it down to 5 and miss things until they are right on top of the camera.

Overall good to keep track of small entry ways, but not much else

title: NOT a subwoofer.
text: This is NOT a subwoofer. This speaker will simply be an additional speaker to your existing system. And, a poor one at that. I returned it after just a few days of trying everything to tune and adjust it. My stock car stereo speakers have deeper bass than the Kenwood. It sounds weak and tinny (not tiny, but, that too). It sounds like it's working way too hard, even at low volumes. It distorts easily with a punchy, popping sound. It was installed properly, and all of my system's settings were correct, but it just wasn't up to the task. The sound from this speaker was, quite frankly, annoying, adding a weak, not quite bass tone, that was hard to listen to. In short, this speaker was a complete disappointment. I did give it two stars however, as it appears well built, came with everything required to install it, and the remote is quite nice and functional, although the blue lights on the remote do nothing but blind you to seeing what you're doing with it if using it at night. I would not recommend this speaker.

title: Took over a thousand pictures so I thought it was good to go and left it for several weeks with ...
text:
Camera only worked for a weekend. I obviously used AA batteries and I also had the solar panel hooked up. Took over a thousand pictures so I thought it was good to go and left it for several weeks with the solar panel in direct sunlight. I came back and only had 3 pictures and over a 1,000 pounds of corn gone. This is very frustrating! Spend top dollar on a camera and expect it to have great pictures or at least some pictures! I'm returning both the camera and the solar panel and going with a different brand. I tested new AA batteries without the solar panel and they lasted less than a day with no pictures taken. I checked that the AC adapter was turned to off and used the quick setup mode.

Update: I am now on my 3rd replacement camera. First one was sucking the batteries down like crazy. Second one had a lens issue. Third one would take a few pictures and then turn itself off even with 100% battery and the 4th one did the same. Is anyone using the solar panel on this? I'm trying to figure out why I am having so many problems. My next unit I'm going to try without the solar panel. I have a cheap $40 camera mounted next to this and it hasn't missed a beat. The pics are lower quality, but it works. Only reason I keep getting replacements is because I could not return for a refund. Moultrie customer service is great, but this model camera just isn't working for me. I've never had issues with moultrie until now.

text: Omnihil is clever and a bit deceiving in that they do not show the plug in the photo. This 5VDC wall wart has a standard 5.5mm X 2.5mm connector with an 'Olympus-specific' adapter plugged onto it. That makes the plug unnecessarily long. Fortunately the LS-10 has it's power jack on the bottom so it is not too bad for my application. Connection cord construction is longer and heavier than usual. I am not sure the thicker cord is an advantage as it adds unnecessary stiffness to what is typically a hand held or tripod mounted device. I'm using this mostly as a line input studio recorder sitting flat on a table, so this adapter works for me, but it might not work well for your application. Unfortunately, the OEM adapter is horrifically overpriced or I would be sending this one back.
